d888e678f1d2fcd8e19565c7f47783beaaffacac.title: Policy support preservation
d888e678f1d2fcd8e19565c7f47783beaaffacac.body:
Let \(P\), \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\), \(x\), and \(\delta\) satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\).
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} \(J\ge 1\), \(0<\beta\), \(0\le \kappa\), \(0<L\), \(0<c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\le 1/J\), \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum and threshold.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(0\le \delta\le \bar\delta\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for conditional-treatment almost every \(a\) in stratum \(x\), the clamped value \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:clamp-policy}\) is a support point of the conditional natural-treatment law given \(X=x\): every open neighborhood \(U\) of \(d_\delta(a)\) has positive conditional-treatment measure in stratum \(x\),
\[
0<\Pr_P(A\in U\mid X=x).
\]

2e9d25a9746c484722687c3716214581a072a0a8.title: Clamp pushforward decomposition
2e9d25a9746c484722687c3716214581a072a0a8.body:
Let \(J\) be a positive integer, let \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfy \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and let \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:clamp-policy}\). Suppose the constants satisfy:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smoothness and thinning.)} \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq 0\), \(L>0\), and \(0<c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum mass.)} \(0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and level.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Evaluation point.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\).
\end{itemize}
Define the lower-tail atom mass
\[
q_x(\delta)=\int_{[0,\delta]}\pi_x(a)\,da .
\]
Then the conditional pushforward law of the clamped treatment satisfies
\[
P\{d_\delta(A)\in da\mid X=x\}
=
P\{A\in da,\ A\in(\delta,1]\mid X=x\}
+
q_x(\delta)\,\delta_\delta(da),
\]
and the atom mass obeys
\[
\frac{c_-\,\delta^{\kappa+1}}{\kappa+1}
\leq
q_x(\delta)
\leq
\frac{c_+\,\delta^{\kappa+1}}{\kappa+1}.
\]

97d0c7fc906d7b5a6ce32e83c0f50ee58d70f975.title: Causal bridge identity
97d0c7fc906d7b5a6ce32e83c0f50ee58d70f975.body:
Let \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) satisfy \(\cref{obj:def:full-data-model-class}\), let \(P\) be its observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin, and let \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) be the clamp map in \(\cref{obj:def:clamp-policy}\).  Suppose the frontier constants satisfy
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Strata.)} \(J\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness and thinning.)} \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq 0\), and \(L>0\).
\item \textbf{(Density and mass constants.)} \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), and \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and coverage levels.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
For \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(a\in[0,1]\), define the full-data response mean
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)
=
P^{\mathrm F}(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x\}} g_x(a,U)\,dP^{\mathrm F}.
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\),
\[
P(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x,\ A\in B\}} Y\,dP^{\mathrm F}
=
\int_B m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\pi_x(a)\,da.
\]
Moreover, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every \(a\in[0,\bar\delta]\),
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mu_x^P(a).
\]
Consequently, for every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the following identities hold:
\[
d_\delta(a)\in \operatorname{supp}\{\pi_x(a)\,da\text{ on }[0,1]\}
\quad
\text{for each }x\in\mathcal X\text{ and for conditional-treatment-a.e. }a,
\]
\[
Y(d_\delta(A))
=
Y\mathbf 1\{\delta<A\}+Y(\delta)\mathbf 1\{A\leq\delta\}
\quad P^{\mathrm F}\text{-a.s.},
\]
and, with
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\int Y(d_\delta(A))\,dP^{\mathrm F},
\qquad
\nu_\delta(P)=\int Y\mathbf 1\{\delta<A\}\,dP,
\qquad
q_x(\delta)=\int_0^\delta \pi_x(a)\,da,
\]
the causal clamp mean equals the observed clamp target
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\nu_\delta(P)+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)
=
\theta_\delta(P).
\]

9664c3e2edfc04c528d0e908746ce9c6b3fb057e.title: Bandwidth phase bounds
9664c3e2edfc04c528d0e908746ce9c6b3fb057e.body:
There exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{bal}},C_{\mathrm{bal}},c_{\mathrm{far}},C_{\mathrm{far}}\) with
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{bal}}\le C_{\mathrm{bal}},
\qquad
0<c_{\mathrm{far}}\le C_{\mathrm{far}},
\]
such that the following assertions hold.  Let
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}
=
n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)} .
\]
For every \(J\), every observed law \(P\), every \(L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\alpha\), and every deterministic sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\), suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} \(J\ge1\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\ge0\), \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), \(p_{\min}\le 1/J\), \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Thinning.)} The law \(P\) satisfies the polynomial thinning condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}\) with exponent \(\kappa\) and constants \(c_-,c_+\).
\item \textbf{(Thresholds.)} \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\) for \((n,\delta_n,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta)\).  Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{bal}}
\le
n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa
\le
C_{\mathrm{bal}},
\]
and
\[
c_{\mathrm{bal}}h_n^{-2\beta}
\le
n h_n(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa
\le
C_{\mathrm{bal}}h_n^{-2\beta}.
\]
If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}\to\infty\), then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{far}}\bigl(n\delta_n^\kappa\bigr)^{-1/(2\beta+1)}
\le
h_n
\le
C_{\mathrm{far}}\bigl(n\delta_n^\kappa\bigr)^{-1/(2\beta+1)} .
\]

Moreover, for every \(D>0\), there exist constants \(c_{\mathrm{near}},C_{\mathrm{near}}\), depending on \(D\), with
\[
0<c_{\mathrm{near}}\le C_{\mathrm{near}},
\]
such that, under the same regime-constant, thinning, and threshold conditions, if
\[
|\delta_n|\le D|\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}|
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
c_{\mathrm{near}}n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)}
\le
h_n
\le
C_{\mathrm{near}}n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)} .
\]

e7cfa8fc6cc9c202641b258b6447b76804675d28.title: Total Gram stabilization
e7cfa8fc6cc9c202641b258b6447b76804675d28.body:
Let \(J\) and \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\) satisfy the standing regime conditions
\[
J\geq 1,\quad \beta>0,\quad \kappa\geq 0,\quad L>0,\quad
0<c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\quad
0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J,\quad 0<\bar\delta<1,\quad 0<\alpha<1/2.
\]
Set \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\) and define the population Gram constant
\[
\lambda_\star
=
\frac{c_-}{c_+}\inf\Bigl\{q:\ \exists \rho\geq 0
\text{ such that }q=\lambda_{\min}\bigl(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\bigr)\Bigr\},
\]
where \(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\) is the reference moment matrix. Then there are constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on these regime constants, such that \(\lambda_\star>0\) and the following holds.

For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), every sample size \(n\) satisfying the sampling condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), every deterministic three-way split \(I_0,I_1,I_2\) with each block having size at least \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\) and with the three blocks pairwise disjoint, every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), and every \(x\in\mathcal X\), let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\). For a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), write
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta}{h_n},\qquad
N_x=\#\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ A_i\in[\delta,\delta+h_n]\},
\]
and let \(G_x\) be the corresponding local monomial Gram matrix on \(I_2\). Define the good-design event
\[
\Omega_x
=
\left\{
N_x>0
\ \text{and}\
\frac{\lambda_\star N_x}{2}\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}v_j^2
\leq
v^\top G_x v
\ \text{for every }v\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}
\right\}.
\]
Then, under the product sampling law \(P^{\otimes n}\),
\[
P^{\otimes n}(\Omega_x^c)
\leq
C\exp\{-c\,n\,h_n(\delta+h_n)^\kappa\}.
\]
Moreover, for every realization \(z\in\Omega_x\), the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) on \(I_2\) reproduce monomials through degree \(\ell\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix}u_i^j
=
\begin{cases}
1, & j=0,\\
0, & 1\leq j\leq \ell,
\end{cases}
\]
and satisfy
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|\leq C,
\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\leq \frac{C}{N_x}.
\]

9eda3283f25541387c7e91ff2b29138de313c6f4.title: Minimax risk frontier
9eda3283f25541387c7e91ff2b29138de313c6f4.body:
Fix \(J,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\) such that
\[
J>0,\quad \beta>0,\quad \kappa\ge 0,\quad L>0,\quad c_->0,\quad
c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+,\quad p_{\min}>0,\quad p_{\min}\le 1/J,\quad
0<\bar\delta<1,\quad 0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
Then there are constants \(c<C\) and an amplitude \(a\) such that
\[
0<c<C,\qquad 0<a\le 1/4 .
\]
For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\ge 1}\) with
\[
0\le \delta_n\le \bar\delta\qquad\text{for every }n,
\]
and for every deterministic sequence \(B_\bullet=(B_n)_{n\ge 1}\) of three split blocks
\(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) with
\[
|I_{0,n}|,|I_{1,n}|,|I_{2,n}|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor
\]
and \(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n}\) pairwise disjoint, the following statements hold for all sufficiently large \(n\). Let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\) evaluated at \(\delta_n\), and let
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
as in \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\). If \(R_n^\star(\delta_n)\) denotes the minimax absolute-error risk over \(\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and if
\[
\mathcal R_{n,B_n}(\delta_n)
=
\sup_{\substack{P\in\mathcal M\\ O_1,\ldots,O_n\ \mathrm{i.i.d.}\ P}}
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\left|\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|
\right],
\]
where the i.i.d. sampling condition is the one in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), then
\[
c r_n
\le R_n^\star(\delta_n)
\le \mathcal R_{n,B_n}(\delta_n)
\le C r_n .
\]
Moreover, the lower bound is witnessed in the following two ways.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Global shift.)} There exist \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\) such that \(P_0\) and \(P_1\) have the same clamp design, both have Bernoulli outcome laws, and
\[
\mu_x^{P_1}(u)=\mu_x^{P_0}(u)+n^{-1/2}
\qquad\text{for every }x\text{ and every }u\in[0,1].
\]
They obey
\[
c n^{-1/2}
\le
\left|\theta_{\delta_n}(P_1)-\theta_{\delta_n}(P_0)\right|,
\qquad
\chi^2(P_1^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n})\le C .
\]
\item \textbf{(Localized perturbation.)} There exist \(Q_0,Q_1\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\) such that \(Q_0\) and \(Q_1\) form a localized Bernoulli regression perturbation at threshold \(\delta_n\), bandwidth \(h_n\), smoothness \(\beta\), and amplitude \(a\). They obey
\[
c\,\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\le
\left|\theta_{\delta_n}(Q_1)-\theta_{\delta_n}(Q_0)\right|,
\qquad
\chi^2(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n})\le C .
\]
\end{itemize}

5cb5df383fdc7ed14565a3f4322eac550eaccdcd.title: Honest length equivalence
5cb5df383fdc7ed14565a3f4322eac550eaccdcd.body:
Fix constants \(J,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Strata and smoothness.)} \(J\geq 1\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq 0\), and \(L>0\).
\item \textbf{(Density and mass constants.)} \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), and \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and coverage levels.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then there are constants \(c\) and \(C\), with \(0<c<C\), such that the following holds. For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfying \(0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta\) for every \(n\), and for every deterministic sequence \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) of three pairwise disjoint split blocks with \(|I_{j,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(j=0,1,2\), all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy the following conclusions.

Let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), evaluated at \(\delta_n\), and let \(r_n\) be the frontier radius from \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\),
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta .
\]
For the honest interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) constructed from the split \(B_n\), the worst-case coverage over the observed clamp model \(\mathcal M\) is at least \(1-\alpha\):
\[
1-\alpha
\leq
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}
P^{\otimes n}\!\left\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in \mathrm{CI}_n\right\},
\]
where \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) is the observed lower-threshold clamp target at threshold \(\delta_n\). Its worst-case expected length is of exact order \(r_n\):
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)\right]
\leq
C\,r_n .
\]
Moreover, the minimax honest expected length satisfies the same lower bound,
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
L_n^\star,
\]
and, more generally, every observed-sample confidence procedure \(C_n\) with measurable interval values and uniform coverage
\[
1-\alpha
\leq
P^{\otimes n}\!\left\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\right\}
\quad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal M
\]
has worst-case expected length at least \(c\,r_n\):
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[
\operatorname{len}\{C_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\}
\right].
\]

c034d4bbe38d1c7b2378a9ef7341e2fb61948978.title: Phase diagram
c034d4bbe38d1c7b2378a9ef7341e2fb61948978.body:
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\) and let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Dimension.)} \(J>0\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness and thinning.)} \(\beta>0\) and \(\kappa\ge 0\).
\item \textbf{(Model constants.)} \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), and \(p_{\min}\le 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope and level.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Define
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}
=
n^{-1/\{2(\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1)\}},
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}
=
n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)} .
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}{\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}}\to\infty .
\]
Moreover, for every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\ge1}\) with
\[
\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\qquad\text{for every }n,
\]
let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), let
\[
a_n=\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta,
\qquad
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
as in \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\). The following conclusions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular regime.)} If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Critical regime.)} For every \(c_0>0\), if \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to c_0\), then
\[
a_n\asymp n^{-1/2},
\qquad
r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Atom-dominated shrinking regime.)} If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to\infty\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp
\delta_n^{\kappa+1}
\bigl(n\delta_n^\kappa\bigr)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Fixed-threshold regime.)} For every \(\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), if \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Zero-threshold target.)} For every \(n\) and every law \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\),
\[
q_x(0)=\int_{[0,0]}\pi_x(a)\,da=0\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X,
\]
\[
\theta_0(P)=\int Y\,dP,
\qquad
n^{-1/2}+0^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta=n^{-1/2},
\]
where the last identity uses the information-balance bandwidth at threshold \(0\).
\item \textbf{(Zero-threshold estimator.)} For every \(n\), every law \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and every admissible split \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\), the total-Gram estimator at threshold \(0\) and bandwidth \(h_n\) agrees \(P^{\otimes n}\)-almost surely with the unit-clipped average of \(Y\) over the first split block:
\[
\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B}(Z;0,h_n)
=
\operatorname{clip}_{[0,1]}\!\left(\frac{1}{|I_0|}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\right).
\]
\item \textbf{(Zero-threshold stabilized guarantees.)} For every deterministic sequence \(B_\bullet=(B_n)_{n\ge1}\) of admissible split blocks, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\operatorname{coverage}_{n,B_n}(0),
\]
and the stabilized worst-case risk and expected length satisfy
\[
\operatorname{risk}_{n,B_n}(0)\asymp n^{-1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{length}_{n,B_n}(0,\alpha)\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]
\end{itemize}

28ed9ad97e77cabadb72374b69ccc6a4457fe256.title: One-cell calibration
28ed9ad97e77cabadb72374b69ccc6a4457fe256.body:
Let \(\bar\delta\in(0,1)\), and let \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) be a deterministic threshold sequence satisfying
\[
0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta
\qquad\text{for every }n .
\]
Assume that \(\delta_n\gg n^{-1/4}\), in the sense that
\[
\frac{\delta_n}{n^{-1/4}}\longrightarrow\infty .
\]
In the one-stratum model with \(\beta=\kappa=1\) and \(\pi(a)=2a\), let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\) evaluated at \((\delta_n,1,1,\bar\delta)\). For the concrete localized Bernoulli alternatives, define
\[
K_n
=
n\int_0^1
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
\operatorname{Bernoulli}(m_{1,\delta_n,h_n}(a)),
\operatorname{Bernoulli}(m_0(a))
\right)\,2a\,da
\]
and
\[
\Delta_n
=
\int_{\delta_n}^1
\bigl(m_{1,\delta_n,h_n}(a)-m_0(a)\bigr)\,2a\,da
+
\left(\int_0^{\delta_n}2a\,da\right)
\bigl(m_{1,\delta_n,h_n}(\delta_n)-m_0(\delta_n)\bigr).
\]
Then
\[
h_n\asymp (n\delta_n)^{-1/3},
\qquad
K_n\asymp n\delta_n h_n^3,
\qquad
\Delta_n\asymp \delta_n^2h_n.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\delta_n\asymp n^{-1/10}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\Delta_n\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]

ac919bc3f2ff436177f83ea3b3150028bd0d441d.title: Observed margin surjectivity
ac919bc3f2ff436177f83ea3b3150028bd0d441d.body:
Fix \(J\in\mathbb N\) and constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} \(0<J\), \(0<\beta\), \(0\leq \kappa\), \(0<L\), \(0<c_-\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\), \(\kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\), \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), \(0<\bar\delta<1\), and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\item \textbf{(Observed model.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) means that \(P\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\).
\item \textbf{(Full-data model.)} \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) means that \(P^{\mathrm F}\) satisfies \(\cref{obj:def:full-data-model-class}\) with constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(P\in\mathcal M\), there exists \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) whose observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is exactly \(P\). Hence the observed-margin map from \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) onto \(\mathcal M\) is surjective.

Moreover, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\) and every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the causal frontier criteria in \(\cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria}\) satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm F}^{\star}(\delta)=R_n^\star(\delta)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm F}^{\star}(\delta,\alpha)=L_n^\star(\delta,\alpha).
\]
Here \(R_n^\star(\delta)\) is the infimum, over observed-measurable estimators with values in \([0,1]\), of the worst-case absolute-error risk over \(P\in\mathcal M\) for the observed clamp target at threshold \(\delta\), and \(L_n^\star(\delta,\alpha)\) is the infimum, over uniformly honest observed-measurable confidence procedures at level \(1-\alpha\), of the worst-case expected interval length over \(P\in\mathcal M\).

92574d86c5b78b15e6d0218c2c218add45b093de.title: Unique continuous regression extension
92574d86c5b78b15e6d0218c2c218add45b093de.body:
Let \(J\) be a positive integer, let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) be a continuity-only observed clamp model with these constants, as in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} The constants satisfy
\[
0\leq \kappa,\qquad
0<c_-,\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\qquad
0<p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Continuous versions.)} For \(r=1,2\), \(\mu_r:\mathcal X\times\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) satisfies that \(a\mapsto \mu_r(x,a)\) is continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\item \textbf{(Regression version property.)} For \(r=1,2\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X,A]=\mu_r(X,A)
\quad\text{\(P\)-almost surely.}
\]
\end{itemize}
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[
\mu_1(x,a)=\mu_2(x,a)
\qquad\text{for every }a\in[0,\bar\delta].
\]

4bd861787cc58df4fe1df7b342b8a6d74fbe9123.title: Causal frontier lift
4bd861787cc58df4fe1df7b342b8a6d74fbe9123.body:
Fix \(J,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\) satisfying the standing regime conditions
\[
J\geq 1,\quad \beta>0,\quad \kappa\geq0,\quad L>0,\quad
0<c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\quad
0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J,\quad 0<\bar\delta<1,\quad 0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\), depending only on these declared constants, such that \(0<c<C\) and the following holds.  For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with
\[
0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta\qquad\text{for every }n,
\]
and every deterministic split-block sequence \(B_\bullet=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\), where each \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) consists of three pairwise disjoint blocks in \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with each block of size at least \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy the following conclusions.  Let
\[
h_n=h_n(\delta_n;\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta)
\]
be the information-balance bandwidth of \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), and let
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
be the frontier rate of \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\).  Let \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) be the causal minimax absolute-error risk and causal minimax honest expected length in \(\cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria}\).

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Estimator.)} The total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) formed from the split \(B_n\), order \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), thinning exponent \(\kappa\), constants \(c_-,c_+\), threshold \(\delta_n\), and bandwidth \(h_n\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\), is observed-sample measurable.
\item \textbf{(Interval.)} The bias-aware closed interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) formed from the split \(B_n\), order \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+\), threshold \(\delta_n\), bandwidth \(h_n\), and level \(\alpha\), has observed-sample measurable ordered endpoints.
\item \textbf{(Risk.)} The estimator attains the causal frontier up to the constants:
\[
c r_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\bigl|\widehat\theta_n-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\bigr|
\leq C r_n .
\]
\item \textbf{(Coverage and length.)} The interval is uniformly honest over the causal full-data class and has worst-case expected length of order \(r_n\):
\[
\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}
\bigl\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in \mathrm{CI}_n\bigr\}
\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
\[
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\bigl[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)\bigr]
\leq C r_n .
\]
\item \textbf{(Optimal expected length.)} The causal minimax honest expected length satisfies
\[
c r_n\leq L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\leq C r_n .
\]
\end{itemize}

833606e6a979cb896fc1ba5bb58d3b9c366fc9a4.title: Continuity causal bridge
833606e6a979cb896fc1ba5bb58d3b9c366fc9a4.body:
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\), let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P^{\mathrm F}\) be a full-data law package with observed margin \(P\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Full-data continuity model.)} \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) with constants \((\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} \(J>0\), \(\kappa\geq0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), and \(0<\bar\delta<1\).
\end{itemize}
For each \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(a\in\mathbb R\), define the full-data response mean by
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)
=
P^{\mathrm F}(X=x)^{-1}
\int_{\{X=x\}} g_x(a,U)\,dP^{\mathrm F}.
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every \(a\in[0,\bar\delta]\),
\[
m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(a).
\]
Moreover, if
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\int Y\!\left(d_\delta(A)\right)\,dP^{\mathrm F},
\]
then, for every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\),
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P),
\]
where \(\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\) is the continuity-only clamp functional in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-clamp-functional}\).

6e5b024a8fb055734587b4a01c03463ff2a91197.title: Observed-margin surjectivity
6e5b024a8fb055734587b4a01c03463ff2a91197.body:
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\) and let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that the continuity-regime design constants used in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class,obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class,obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria}\) hold for \((J,\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta)\), and that \(0<\alpha<1/2\).

Then the observed-margin map from \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) onto \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) is surjective: for every \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), there exists \(P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) whose observed margin is \(P\). Moreover, for every \(n\in\mathbb N\) and every \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\), the four continuity-frontier criteria of \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria}\), evaluated at \((J,n,\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\delta,\alpha)\), satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star .
\]

717a8f30661923ed502307e1f1c5b29d9a4c0549.title: Continuity frontier characterization
717a8f30661923ed502307e1f1c5b29d9a4c0549.body:
Fix \(J\in\mathbb N\) and constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose the continuity-design constants satisfy the declared continuity-only regime conditions, including \(0<\alpha<1/2\). Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\) with \(0<c<C\) such that the following statements hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Uniform frontier bounds.)} For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for all \(n\), and for every deterministic sequence \(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy the following bounds. With
\[
s_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1},
\]
and with \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\), \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\), \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star\), and \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria}\),
\[
c s_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\right|
\leq C s_n,
\]
the interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\) has uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\), its worst-case expected length is at most \(C s_n\), and
\[
c s_n\leq L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star.
\]
Moreover,
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star=L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star,
\]
and the same estimator and interval satisfy
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F}_{\mathrm{obs}})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|
\leq C s_n,
\]
with causal coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) and causal worst-case expected length at most \(C s_n\).

\item \textbf{(Elbow and null-threshold rates.)} For the continuity-only rate in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-frontier}\),
\[
s_n\bigl(\delta_n=n^{-1/(2(\kappa+1))}\bigr)
\asymp n^{-1/2},
\qquad
s_n(0)\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Fixed positive thresholds.)} For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for all \(n\), every \(\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), and \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\),
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star \not\to 0,
\qquad
L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star \not\to 0.
\]
\end{itemize}

7c218bd7d919969d85d8a8c887da589b49884b38.title: I.i.d. sampling
7c218bd7d919969d85d8a8c887da589b49884b38.body: The observed units \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P\).

2321a62a59583d0d4a73049b92f35746d78ba49a.title: Conditional treatment density
2321a62a59583d0d4a73049b92f35746d78ba49a.body:
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\),
\[
P(A\in B\mid X=x)=\int_B \pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da .
\]

6a5f4918fa2841274f80adae9253a4301bea8024.title: Structural consistency
6a5f4918fa2841274f80adae9253a4301bea8024.body:
Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent response.)} The latent response variable \(U\) takes values in \(\mathcal U\).
\item \textbf{(Structural maps.)} For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the map
\[
g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1]
\]
is jointly Borel measurable.
\item \textbf{(Potential and observed outcomes.)} There is a single \(P^{\mathrm F}\)-null set outside which, for every \(a\in[0,1]\),
\[
Y(a)=g_X(a,U),
\qquad
Y=g_X(A,U).
\]
\end{itemize}

b41dc9ae41dde77161ff2d588e81c62667d2e237.title: Conditional exchangeability
b41dc9ae41dde77161ff2d588e81c62667d2e237.body: Under \(P^{\mathrm F}\), the treatment \(A\) and latent response variable \(U\) are conditionally independent given \(X\).

bd04c0a0aaa53fd95ba46aee6f223d688844365e.title: Polynomial overlap thinning
bd04c0a0aaa53fd95ba46aee6f223d688844365e.body:
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and for Lebesgue-almost every \(a\in[0,1]\),
\[
c_- a^\kappa \leq \pi_x(a) \leq c_+ a^\kappa .
\]

b48edf5322b19adac2ac93e66977134d8184e6f4.title: Hölder regression extension
b48edf5322b19adac2ac93e66977134d8184e6f4.body:
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), an almost-everywhere version of the conditional mean \(a\mapsto \mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) admits a continuous extension, the regression extension \(\mu_x^P\), such that for all \(s,t\in[0,1]\),
\[
\left|\mu_x^P(t)-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}\frac{(\mu_x^P)^{(j)}(s)}{j!}(t-s)^j\right|
\leq L|t-s|^\beta .
\]

9130bf1eaeeadda0089294061fa5e695736f16a0.title: Full-data response continuity
9130bf1eaeeadda0089294061fa5e695736f16a0.body: Under the full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\), for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the full-data response mean \(a\mapsto m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\) is continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\).

4d3ade8455ffd02eb3cf51d7fce3479e5da78c2c.title: Observed law class \(\mathcal M\)
4d3ade8455ffd02eb3cf51d7fce3479e5da78c2c.body:
The observed law class \(\mathcal M\) is
\[
\mathcal M
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])
:
P\text{ satisfies }\cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning,obj:ass:holder-regression}
\right\}.
\]

88a4e7d387998d6e2ba7e2ed87926c636e6793d2.title: Clamp policy \(d_\delta\) and \(A^\delta\)
88a4e7d387998d6e2ba7e2ed87926c636e6793d2.body:
For \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), the lower-threshold clamp map \(d_\delta\) and the clamped treatment \(A^\delta\) are
\[
d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\},
\qquad
A^\delta=d_\delta(A).
\]

35e7267143269fc411d8f0cdc4ae0b0f77cd70f9.title: Bandwidth \(h_n\)
35e7267143269fc411d8f0cdc4ae0b0f77cd70f9.body:
The information-balance bandwidth \(h_n\) for \(\delta_n\) is
\[
h_n
=
\inf\left\{
h\in(0,1-\bar\delta]:
n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h)^\kappa\geq 1
\right\},
\]
with \(h_n=1-\bar\delta\) when the displayed set is empty.

0b7e67e5a9d50df60ddb5ab2ffadc60d72349e22.title: Frontier rate \(r_n\)
0b7e67e5a9d50df60ddb5ab2ffadc60d72349e22.body:
The Hölder minimax rate \(r_n\) is
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta .
\]

d4e1ecc13b7c626cd4c91c65682e35bab5a89daa.title: Total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\)
d4e1ecc13b7c626cd4c91c65682e35bab5a89daa.body:
Given deterministic split blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\), the threshold \(\delta_n\), and the weights \(w_{ix}\), define \(\widehat\theta_n\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the retained-course empirical mean
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
|I_0|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the empirical lower-threshold atom mass
\[
\widehat b_x
=
|I_1|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ A_i\leq\delta_n\}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the clipped local-polynomial estimate with atom fallback by
\[
\widetilde\mu_x
=
\begin{cases}
\Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i\right),& \Omega_x,\\
1/2,& \Omega_x^c.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Output the total-Gram clamp-target estimator
\[
\widehat\theta_n
=
\Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left[
\widehat\nu_n+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x
\right].
\]
\end{enumerate}

6c701ec0452ec4a3af9f6657543d9d32605ba0fb.title: Honest interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\)
6c701ec0452ec4a3af9f6657543d9d32605ba0fb.body:
Given the estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\), split blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\), threshold \(\delta_n\), bandwidth \(h_n\), weights \(w_{ix}\), and confidence level \(1-\alpha\), define \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the Hoeffding calibration multiplier
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}.
\]
\item Define the split-block stochastic-error radii
\[
b_0=\frac{t_\alpha}{\sqrt{|I_0|}},
\qquad
b_1=\frac{t_\alpha}{\sqrt{|I_1|}}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the local regression bias-plus-variance radius
\[
B_x
=
Lh_n^\beta\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|
+
t_\alpha\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the atom-weighted interval contribution
\[
D_x
=
\begin{cases}
(\widehat b_x+b_1)B_x+b_1,& \Omega_x,\\
\widehat b_x+b_1,& \Omega_x^c.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Output the bias-aware honest interval
\[
\mathrm{CI}_n
=
\left[
\widehat\theta_n-b_0-\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_x,\,
\widehat\theta_n+b_0+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_x
\right]\cap[0,1].
\]
\end{enumerate}

42ebcd33c3746bc34e849d600e5b2339e05082e8.title: Exact-modulus handle \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\)
42ebcd33c3746bc34e849d600e5b2339e05082e8.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), a split block \(I_2\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\ell\), \(\beta\), \(\kappa\), \(L\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(p_{\min}\), \(\delta_n\), \(h_n>0\), and \(t\geq0\), define
\[
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t)
=
\int \operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes n})(z).
\]
Here \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\) is a realized observed design under the \(n\)-fold independent observed-design law induced by \(P\). For this design, define
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
The affine weights reproducing monomials at the threshold are
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=
\left\{w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}:
w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\ 
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
Let \(V_{z,x}\) be the realized local monomial design matrix with row \(v_\ell(u_i)^\top\) for \(i\in S_{z,x}\). Equivalently, the affine constraints are
\[
V_{z,x}^\top w_{S_{z,x}}=e_0,
\]
and the associated total Gram is
\[
G_x=V_{z,x}^\top V_{z,x}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) that are continuous and satisfy
\[
\left|f(a')-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}f^{(j)}(a)(a'-a)^j/j!\right|
\leq
L|a'-a|^\beta
\quad\text{for every }a,a'\in[0,1],
\]
where the derivatives are the intrinsic derivatives on \([0,1]\) used in the declared Hölder condition. For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define
\[
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
=
\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)\right|,
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w)
=
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
+
t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The realized exact modulus is the real-valued totalization
\[
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)
=
\begin{cases}
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w),&\mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\
0,&\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Finally, with
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2},
\]
define
\[
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t_\alpha).
\]
The constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\) enter through the corresponding member conditions of \(\mathcal M\). Both \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) and \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) are radius quantities; an untruncated symmetric interval with such radius has full length twice the radius.

bf180ebb76acc607b0ed63edd8148a2224d85e45.title: Full-data causal class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\)
bf180ebb76acc607b0ed63edd8148a2224d85e45.body:
\(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) is the collection of full-data law packages \(P^{\mathrm F}\) with the following memberwise structure relative to \(\cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:exchangeability,obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent response space.)} Each member carries its own standard Borel latent-response space \(\mathcal U\) and an \(\mathcal U\)-valued random variable \(U\).
\item \textbf{(Structural response maps.)} Each member carries jointly Borel maps
\[
g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1],
\qquad x\in\mathcal X,
\]
and a jointly measurable process
\[
\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Full-data law.)} Each member carries a probability law for
\[
(X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}).
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed margin.)} The \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is some \(P\in\mathcal M\).
\item \textbf{(Causal member conditions.)} Within the member's own carrier, the simultaneous latent-response consistency, latent randomization, and fiberwise structural-mean continuity on \([0,\bar\delta]\) conditions hold.
\end{itemize}
Members may use different standard Borel carriers, and the class is defined memberwise.

0a2bf3ee078140d66a0ac8f90c6ea0a9976d803e.title: Causal frontier criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\)
0a2bf3ee078140d66a0ac8f90c6ea0a9976d803e.body:
For estimators and intervals measurable with respect to the observed sample \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), define the causal minimax absolute-error risk
\[
 R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
 =
 \inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
 \left|\widehat\psi-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|.
\]
Define the causal minimax honest expected length
\[
 L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
 =
 \inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 (P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}
 \sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(C_n)].
\]

4054e376478ebb8611c4e8ca5d536966ab7bebc1.title: Continuity-only model class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\)
4054e376478ebb8611c4e8ca5d536966ab7bebc1.body:
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) is the set of laws
\[
P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])
\]
satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}\) and the following continuity condition: for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), an almost-everywhere version of
\[
a\mapsto \mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]
\]
admits a continuous extension to \([0,\bar\delta]\). The continuity extension is required memberwise for each stratum.

b0d0527d88a2a26dd21c9b2cb2ac794c42a7ae20.title: Continuity clamp functional \(\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\)
b0d0527d88a2a26dd21c9b2cb2ac794c42a7ae20.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}\) and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), define
\[
\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)
=
\mathbb E_P\!\left[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}\right]
+
\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(\delta).
\]

ab38a2ee4c055873f198f9f3e27bb5f8c68caa70.title: Continuity frontier \(s_n\)
ab38a2ee4c055873f198f9f3e27bb5f8c68caa70.body:
Define the continuity-only frontier rate by
\[
s_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}.
\]

f3293e85e9d81e12de253db9e97dc5555b61764c.title: Continuity fallback estimator \(\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\)
f3293e85e9d81e12de253db9e97dc5555b61764c.body:
The inputs are the deterministic split blocks \(I_0,I_1\), the threshold \(\delta_n\), and the observations \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item Define the retained-course empirical mean
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
|I_0|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the empirical lower-threshold atom mass
\[
\widehat b_x
=
|I_1|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\leq\delta_n\}.
\]
\item Output the fixed-regression-fallback estimator
\[
\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}
=
\Pi_{[0,1]}\left\{\widehat\nu_n+\frac12\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\right\}.
\]
\end{enumerate}

7e4a07c3fc9bc910f53a4a8c03a59d1cbd8af4c0.title: Continuity honest interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\)
7e4a07c3fc9bc910f53a4a8c03a59d1cbd8af4c0.body:
The inputs are the split blocks \(I_0,I_1\), the level \(\alpha\), the estimator \(\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}\), and the empirical masses \(\widehat b_x\).
\begin{enumerate}
\item For \(j=0,1\), define the split-specific Hoeffding radius
\[
t_{j,\alpha}
=
\sqrt{\frac{\log(4/\alpha)}{2|I_j|}}.
\]
\item Define the empirical total lower-threshold atom mass
\[
\widehat B_n
=
\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x.
\]
\item Output the Hoeffding interval
\[
\mathrm{CI}_{n,\mathrm{cont}}
=
\left[
\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}-t_{0,\alpha}-t_{1,\alpha}-\frac12\widehat B_n,\,
\widehat\theta_{n,\mathrm{cont}}+t_{0,\alpha}+t_{1,\alpha}+\frac12\widehat B_n
\right]\cap[0,1].
\]
\end{enumerate}

562ee99f836b2e4f2f2cdc41a70c0bc7fe7a32fa.title: Continuity full-data class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\)
562ee99f836b2e4f2f2cdc41a70c0bc7fe7a32fa.body:
Define \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}\) as the collection of full-data law packages \(P^{\mathrm F}\) with a memberwise standard Borel latent-response space \(\mathcal U\), latent variable \(U\), jointly Borel stratum-specific response maps \(g_x\), and jointly measurable potential-outcome process \(\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}\), such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed margin.)} The observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin of \(P^{\mathrm F}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Consistency.)} The package satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:consistency}\).
\item \textbf{(Exchangeability.)} The package satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:exchangeability}\).
\item \textbf{(Response continuity.)} The package satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity}\).
\end{itemize}
The carrier spaces \(\mathcal U\) may vary with \(P^{\mathrm F}\).

dcfbd6cecf98dccca519262f1e37c8dd1152ab6b.title: Continuity frontier criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star\)
dcfbd6cecf98dccca519262f1e37c8dd1152ab6b.body:
For estimators and intervals measurable with respect to \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\), define the continuity-only observed minimax absolute-error risk by
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
=
\inf_{\widehat\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta-\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\right|.
\]
Define the continuity-only observed minimax honest expected length by
\[
L_{n,\mathrm{cont}}^\star
=
\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}P^{\otimes n}
\{\theta_{\delta_n,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\operatorname{len}(C_n)\right].
\]
For the full-data continuity-only class, define the causal minimax absolute-error risk by
\[
R_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
\inf_{\widehat\psi}\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\psi-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|.
\]
Define the continuity-only causal minimax honest expected length by
\[
L_{n,\mathrm{cont},\mathrm F}^\star
=
\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha}
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}\!\left[\operatorname{len}(C_n)\right].
\]

0fc938260405c121feb3907889189be772b1f26c.title: Sharp constant exact-modulus frontier
0fc938260405c121feb3907889189be772b1f26c.body:
A natural sharp-constant question is whether the following simultaneous calibration can be achieved. Fix the declared regime constants. Is there a constant \(c>0\) such that, for every admissible deterministic threshold sequence \(\delta_{\bullet}=(\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfying
\[
\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to\lambda
\]
for some \(\lambda\in[0,\infty]\), there is a deterministic sequence \(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, allowed to depend on the full threshold sequence and chosen independently of the realized data, with the following properties?

For a realized observed sample \(z\), let \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)\) be the total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) formed with the three blocks in \(B_n\). In \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}\), interpret the design argument as the \((X,A)\)-projection of \(z\), using the third block in \(B_n\). Define
\[
R_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha),
\qquad
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2},
\]
and
\[
C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\left[
\max\left\{0,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)-R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\},
\min\left\{1,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)+R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\}
\right].
\]
The first requirement is eventual uniform \((1-\alpha)\)-honesty:
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P^{\otimes n}
\left\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right\}
\geq1-\alpha
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), with \(Y\in[0,1]\) and measurable treatment density envelope
\[
c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa .
\]
Writing
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left[\operatorname{len}\!\left(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right)\right],
\]
the sharp-constant length question asks whether
\[
\frac{L_n^\star}{r_n}\longrightarrow c,
\qquad
\frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{r_n}\longrightarrow c .
\]

Finally, let
\[
W_{n,B_n}=\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha),
\]
where the worst integrated radius is computed with the third block in \(B_n\). Is there a fixed constant \(D>0\), a fixed amplitude \(\mathsf{amplitude}\) with \(0<\mathsf{amplitude}\leq1/4\), and sequences
\[
P_0,P_{\mathrm{reg}},P_{\mathrm{loc}}:\mathbb N\to\mathcal M
\]
such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the following conditions hold?
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model membership.)} The laws \(P_0(n)\), \(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)\), and \(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)\) satisfy the declared ClampModel member conditions.
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} Their \(n\)-sample experiments are independent product experiments under the corresponding observed law.
\item \textbf{(Regular perturbation.)} The pair \((P_0(n),P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n))\) satisfies the declared global Bernoulli shift at scale \(n^{-1/2}\).
\item \textbf{(Localized perturbation.)} The pair \((P_0(n),P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n))\) satisfies the declared localized Bernoulli perturbation at \(\beta\), \(\delta_n\),
\[
h_n,
\]
and \(\mathsf{amplitude}\), where \(h_n\) is the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\).
\item \textbf{(Chi-square bounds.)}
\[
\chi^2\!\left(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)^{\otimes n}\middle\Vert P_0(n)^{\otimes n}\right)\leq D,
\qquad
\chi^2\!\left(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)^{\otimes n}\middle\Vert P_0(n)^{\otimes n}\right)\leq D .
\]
\end{itemize}
For these witnesses, define
\[
\Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}
=
\left|\theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)\right)-
          \theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_0(n)\right)\right|
+
\left|\theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)\right)-
          \theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_0(n)\right)\right|.
\]
The matching-limit question is whether
\[
\frac{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
\qquad
\frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
\qquad
\frac{2W_{n,B_n}}{L_n^\star}\longrightarrow1 .
\]
Here \(W_{n,B_n}\) is a radius, so \(2W_{n,B_n}\) is the candidate untruncated expected full length. The convention
\[
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)=0
\]
when the affine feasible set is empty remains in force.

c5d4c01f7acad5b6f43814a6b3cd8c6ac7fb29d5.title: Total Gram stabilization
c5d4c01f7acad5b6f43814a6b3cd8c6ac7fb29d5.body:
Let \(J\) be a positive integer and let the declared constants satisfy
\[
\beta>0,\qquad \kappa\ge 0,\qquad L>0,\qquad
0<c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+,\qquad
0<p_{\min}\le 1/J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad 0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
Then there are constants \(C,c>0\), depending only on these declared constants, such that the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant \(\lambda_\star\) in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\), evaluated at \((\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) with \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\), and the following hold.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model and sampling.)} \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are sampled according to \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\).
\item \textbf{(Split and threshold.)} \(I_0,I_1,I_2\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}\) are deterministic, pairwise-disjoint split blocks with \(|I_b|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(b=0,1,2\), and \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and stratum.)} \(h_n\) is the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\) at \((n,\delta,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta)\), and \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\end{itemize}

For the good-design event \(\Omega_x\) in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\),
\[
P^{\otimes n}(\Omega_x^c)
\le
C\exp\{-c\,n\,h_n(\delta+h_n)^\kappa\}.
\]
On \(\Omega_x\), the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\) satisfy, for every \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix} U_i^j
=
\begin{cases}
1, & j=0,\\
0, & j\ge 1,
\end{cases}
\]
and also obey
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|\le C,
\qquad
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\le \frac{C}{N_x}.
\]

abafcba6fd27df4079bdfe40c241dedff9e03269.title: Honest length frontier
abafcba6fd27df4079bdfe40c241dedff9e03269.body:
There are constants \(c,C\in(0,\infty)\), with \(c<C\), for which the following holds.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The number of strata \(J\) is a positive integer, \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq0\), \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), \(\bar\delta\in(0,1)\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold path.)} The deterministic thresholds satisfy \(0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta\) for every \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Sample splits.)} For every \(n\), \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is a deterministic three-way split of the sample indices with pairwise disjoint blocks and \(|I_{j,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(j=0,1,2\).
\end{itemize}

For all sufficiently large \(n\), set \(h_n\) to be the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\) from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), and set
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta .
\]
Then the stabilized interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) has worst-case coverage
\[
\inf\Bigl\{
P^{\otimes n}\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in \mathrm{CI}_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\}:
P\in\mathcal M
\Bigr\}\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
and its worst-case expected length is comparable to \(r_n\):
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
\sup\Bigl\{
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\bigl[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)\bigr]:
P\in\mathcal M
\Bigr\}
\leq
C\,r_n .
\]
Moreover, the minimax honest expected length satisfies
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
L_n^\star,
\]
where \(L_n^\star\) is the infimum, over observed-sample confidence procedures with uniform coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) over \(\mathcal M\), of their worst-case expected length. Equivalently, every observed-sample confidence procedure \(C_n\) with
\[
\inf\Bigl\{
P^{\otimes n}\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\}:
P\in\mathcal M
\Bigr\}\geq 1-\alpha
\]
has worst-case expected length at least \(c\,r_n\):
\[
c\,r_n
\leq
\sup\Bigl\{
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\bigl[\operatorname{len}(C_n)\bigr]:
P\in\mathcal M
\Bigr\}.
\]

b2e982ec2b726b599f5d9bc6892889bb3f7364b3.title: Phase boundary diagram
b2e982ec2b726b599f5d9bc6892889bb3f7364b3.body:
Let \(J\) be a positive integer and let the constants satisfy
\[
\beta>0,\qquad
\kappa\geq 0,\qquad
L>0,\qquad
0<c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\qquad
0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad
0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
Define the two boundary scales
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}
=
n^{-1/\{2(\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1)\}},
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}
=
n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)} .
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}{\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}}\longrightarrow \infty .
\]
Moreover, for every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq 1}\) with
\(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\), let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth in \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), let
\[
a_n=\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta,
\qquad
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
as in \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\). The following conclusions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Regular thresholds.} If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to 0\), then \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\).
\item \textbf{Critical thresholds.} For every \(c_0>0\), if \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to c_0\), then \(a_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\) and \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\).
\item \textbf{Vanishing atom-dominated thresholds.} If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to\infty\) and \(\delta_n\to 0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp
\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\bigl(n\delta_n^\kappa\bigr)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)} .
\]
\item \textbf{Fixed thresholds.} For every \(\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), if \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)} .
\]
\item \textbf{Zero threshold identities.} For every \(n\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\),
\[
q_x(0)=0\quad\text{for every }x,\qquad
\theta_0(P)=\int Y\,dP,\qquad
n^{-1/2}+0^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta=n^{-1/2},
\]
where the last identity uses the bandwidth \(h_n\) at threshold \(0\).
\item \textbf{Zero threshold estimator.} For every \(n\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and every admissible three-way split \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\), the total-Gram estimator in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\), formed at threshold \(0\) with bandwidth \(h_n\), agrees \(P^{\otimes n}\)-almost surely with the clipped empirical mean on the block \(I_0\):
\[
\widehat\theta_n(z)=
\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}\!\left(\frac{1}{|I_0|}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\right).
\]
\item \textbf{Zero threshold stabilized guarantees.} For every deterministic sequence \(B_\bullet=(B_n)_{n\geq 1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, the stabilized zero-threshold procedure has eventual coverage at least \(1-\alpha\), and its stabilized worst-case risk and expected length both satisfy
\[
\operatorname{Risk}_n(B_n,0)\asymp n^{-1/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{Length}_n(B_n,0,\alpha)\asymp n^{-1/2}.
\]
\end{itemize}

39e8b3a07c4ffdddc2e8a86e18f4896b213b7729.title: Causal frontier lift
39e8b3a07c4ffdddc2e8a86e18f4896b213b7729.body:
Let \(J\) be a positive integer, and let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The constants satisfy
\[
\beta>0,\qquad \kappa\geq0,\qquad L>0,\qquad c_->0,\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,
\]
\[
p_{\min}>0,\qquad p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad 0<\alpha<\frac12 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} The deterministic thresholds \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfy
\[
0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta
\]
for every \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Split blocks.)} For each \(n\), \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is a deterministic three-way split with pairwise disjoint blocks and
\[
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{0,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{1,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{2,n}|.
\]
\end{itemize}
Let \(h_n\), the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\), be as in \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), and let
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
be the frontier rate from \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\). Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\), with \(0<c<C\), depending only on the displayed regime constants, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\), formed with split \(B_n\), order \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), bandwidth \(h_n\), and threshold \(\delta_n\), is observed-sample measurable, and the bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) in \(\cref{obj:def:honest-interval}\), formed with the same split, order, bandwidth, and threshold, is an observed-sample measurable interval.

For the causal minimax criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) in \(\cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria}\), the same \(n\) also satisfies
\[
c r_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_n-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|
\leq C r_n,
\]
\[
\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in \mathrm{CI}_n\}
\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
\[
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)
\leq C r_n,
\]
and, in the extended nonnegative real order,
\[
c r_n\leq L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\leq C r_n .
\]

7bd3eff79ee0ecd6cdb21626c7b7fdb2670198f3.title: Minimax clamp frontier
7bd3eff79ee0ecd6cdb21626c7b7fdb2670198f3.body:
Fix \(J,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\) satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime.)} \(J\geq 1\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\geq0\), \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), \(p_{\min}>0\), \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\), \(\bar\delta\in(0,1)\), and \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\).
\item \textbf{(Thresholds.)} The threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) is deterministic and satisfies \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Splits.)} \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is any deterministic sequence of three pairwise-disjoint sample blocks with \(|I_{j,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(j=0,1,2\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exist constants \(0<c<C\) and an amplitude \(a\in(0,1/4]\), depending only on the displayed regime constants, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), with \(h_n\) the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\) and
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
as in \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\), the observed minimax absolute-error risk \(R_n^\star\) over the clamp model \(\mathcal M\) in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) and the worst-case risk of the stabilized estimator using \(B_n\) satisfy
\[
c r_n
\leq
R_n^\star
\leq
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M} \mathbb E_P\!\left[
\left|\widehat\theta_{n,B_n}^{\mathrm{TG}}-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|
\right]
\leq
C r_n .
\]
Moreover, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the lower bound is witnessed inside the same clamp model by:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Global shift.)} Laws \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), sharing the same clamp design, having Bernoulli outcomes, and obeying
\[
\mu_x^{P_1}(a)=\mu_x^{P_0}(a)+n^{-1/2}
\quad\text{for every }x\text{ and }a\in[0,1],
\]
with
\[
c n^{-1/2}
\leq
\left|\theta_{\delta_n}(P_1)-\theta_{\delta_n}(P_0)\right|,
\qquad
\chi^2\!\left(P_1^{\otimes n},P_0^{\otimes n}\right)\leq C .
\]
\item \textbf{(Localized perturbation.)} Laws \(Q_0,Q_1\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\) and forming a localized Bernoulli regression perturbation at threshold \(\delta_n\), bandwidth \(h_n\), exponent \(\beta\), and amplitude \(a\), with
\[
c\,\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\leq
\left|\theta_{\delta_n}(Q_1)-\theta_{\delta_n}(Q_0)\right|,
\qquad
\chi^2\!\left(Q_1^{\otimes n},Q_0^{\otimes n}\right)\leq C .
\]
\end{itemize}

ec250cb8c1e3d7a481763aa75146ebd31cdab3fa.title: Clamp functionals \(q_x(\delta)\), \(\nu_\delta(P)\), and \(\theta_\delta(P)\)
ec250cb8c1e3d7a481763aa75146ebd31cdab3fa.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), define
\[
q_x(\delta)=\int_{[0,\delta]}\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da,
\qquad
\nu_\delta(P)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}\right].
\]
The unsmoothed observed-data clamp target is
\[
\theta_\delta(P)
=
\nu_\delta(P)
+
\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta).
\]

51d088e928f9b8002cffe2c497f1756433f34378.title: Local design quantities \(U_i\), \(G_x\), and \(w_{ix}\)
51d088e928f9b8002cffe2c497f1756433f34378.body:
For a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), the bandwidth \(h_n\) from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), a deterministic third split block \(I_2\), and a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), define
\[
U_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)^\top .
\]
The local count and total Gram matrix are
\[
N_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\},
\]
\[
G_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}
v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top .
\]
Let
\[
M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}
=
\frac{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
\]
and
\[
\lambda_\star
=
\frac{c_-}{c_+}\inf_{\rho\geq0}
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\right).
\]
The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) is
\[
\Omega_x
=
\left\{
N_x>0
\ \text{and}\
v^\top G_xv\geq\frac{\lambda_\star N_x}{2}\lVert v\rVert_2^2
\ \text{for every }v
\right\}.
\]
The exact local-polynomial intercept weight is
\[
w_{ix}
=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}\,
e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i),& \Omega_x,\\
0,& \Omega_x^{c}.
\end{cases}
\]

40c50234c8ad0f233f219f6eb81ec45a7796e71a.title: Total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\)
40c50234c8ad0f233f219f6eb81ec45a7796e71a.body:
Given split blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\) and the local-design quantities in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\), define the estimator as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Compute the retained-course empirical mean
\[
\widehat\nu_n
=
\frac{1}{|I_0|}
\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), compute the empirical lower-threshold atom mass
\[
\widehat b_x
=
\frac{1}{|I_1|}
\sum_{i\in I_1}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ A_i\leq\delta_n\}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), compute the clipped local-polynomial threshold estimate
\[
\widetilde\mu_x
=
\begin{cases}
\Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}Y_i\right),& \Omega_x,\\
1/2,& \Omega_x^{c}.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Output the total-Gram clamp-target estimator
\[
\widehat\theta_n
=
\Pi_{[0,1]}\!\left[
\widehat\nu_n+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x
\right].
\]
\end{enumerate}

2fe1dfe33e86c832efc1a29ecd8f8301ea21ca92.title: Honest interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\)
2fe1dfe33e86c832efc1a29ecd8f8301ea21ca92.body:
Given the local-design quantities in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\), define the interval as follows.
\begin{enumerate}
\item Set the Hoeffding calibration multiplier and split-block stochastic-error radii
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{\log(12J/\alpha)}{2}},
\qquad
b_0=\frac{t_\alpha}{\sqrt{|I_0|}},
\qquad
b_1=\frac{t_\alpha}{\sqrt{|I_1|}}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), set the local regression bias-plus-noise radius
\[
B_x
=
Lh_n^\beta\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|
+
t_\alpha\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
\item For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), set the atom-weighted interval contribution
\[
D_x
=
\begin{cases}
(\widehat b_x+b_1)B_x+b_1,& \Omega_x,\\
\widehat b_x+b_1,& \Omega_x^{c}.
\end{cases}
\]
\item Output the bias-aware honest interval
\[
\mathrm{CI}_n
=
\left[
\widehat\theta_n-b_0-\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_x,\,
\widehat\theta_n+b_0+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_x
\right]\cap[0,1].
\]
\end{enumerate}

e3e7d34d2ce53a017fc57a900372a7aac46ad092.title: Exact-modulus handle \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\)
e3e7d34d2ce53a017fc57a900372a7aac46ad092.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal M\), a split block \(I_2\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\ell\), \(\beta\), \(\kappa\), \(L\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(p_{\min}\), \(\delta_n\), \(h_n>0\), and \(t\geq0\), with \(\mathcal M\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) and local-design notation as in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\), define
\[
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t)
=
\int \operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes n})(z).
\]
For a realized design \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), set
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
S_{z,x}
=
\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
The affine weight set is
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=
\left\{
w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}:
w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
Let \(V_{z,x}\) be the matrix with row \(v_\ell(u_i)^\top\) for \(i\in S_{z,x}\). Equivalently,
\[
V_{z,x}^\top w_{S_{z,x}}=e_0,
\qquad
G_x=V_{z,x}^\top V_{z,x}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of continuous functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) satisfying
\[
\left|f(a')-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}f^{(j)}(a)(a'-a)^j/j!\right|
\leq
L|a'-a|^\beta
\]
for every \(a,a'\in[0,1]\), where the derivatives are the intrinsic derivatives on \([0,1]\) used in the declared Hölder condition. For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define
\[
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
=
\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)
\right|
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w)
=
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
+
t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The realized exact modulus is
\[
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)
=
\begin{cases}
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w),& \mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\
0,& \mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
Finally,
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\frac{\log(12J/\alpha)}{2}},
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t_\alpha).
\]
The quantities \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) and \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) are radius, or half-length, quantities; an untruncated symmetric interval with either radius has full length twice that radius.

d37bb43d285a390232497c8a808e3c6eeb9f41ab.title: Causal clamp mean \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})\)
d37bb43d285a390232497c8a808e3c6eeb9f41ab.body:
For a full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:full-data-model-class}\), the clamp policy \(d_\delta\) from \(\cref{obj:def:clamp-policy}\), and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), define the causal clamp mean by
\[
\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})
=
\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}\!\left[Y(d_\delta(A))\right].
\]

abe5f4e5dac3441f04c3a95b2cda04f73083d7d7.title: Causal frontier criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\)

21c9cafabda26761ca60a9285db24883fd4ea07a.title: Continuity clamp target \(\theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)\)
21c9cafabda26761ca60a9285db24883fd4ea07a.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) and \(0\leq\delta\leq\bar\delta\), with \(q_x(\delta)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:clamp-functional}\) and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}\), define
\[
 \theta_{\delta,\mathrm{cont}}(P)
 =
 \mathbb E_P\!\left[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}\right]
 +
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
 p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P(\delta).
\]

9f0d310701eb839ae72cd3d81c2e06098e03ee62.title: Sharp constant problem
9f0d310701eb839ae72cd3d81c2e06098e03ee62.body:
A natural sharp-constant question for the clamp target in \(\cref{obj:def:clamp-functional}\) is whether the following simultaneous calibration can be achieved. Fix the declared regime constants. Does there exist a constant \(c>0\) such that, for every admissible deterministic threshold sequence \(\delta_{\bullet}=(\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfying
\[
 \frac{\delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}\longrightarrow\lambda
\]
for some \(\lambda\in[0,\infty]\), there exists a deterministic sequence \(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, allowed to depend on the entire threshold sequence and chosen independently of the realized data, with the following properties?

For a realized observed sample \(z\), let \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)\) be the total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) formed with the three blocks in \(B_n\), and interpret the design argument of \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}\) as the \((X,A)\)-projection of \(z\), using the third block in \(B_n\). Put
\[
 R_{n,B_n}(z)
 =
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha),
 \qquad
 t_\alpha
 =
 \sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2},
\]
and define
\[
 C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}(z)
 =
 \left[
 \max\left\{0,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)-R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\},
 \min\left\{1,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)+R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\}
 \right].
\]
Is \(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\) eventually uniformly \((1-\alpha)\)-honest, in the sense that
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P^{\otimes n}
 \left\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right\}
 \geq1-\alpha
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\), while retaining bounded \(Y\) and the measurable envelope
\[
 c_-a^\kappa\leq\pi_x(a)\leq c_+a^\kappa?
\]
If
\[
 \ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
 =
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
 \left[\operatorname{len}\!\left(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right)\right],
\]
do the sharp-constant limits
\[
 \frac{L_n^\star}{r_n}\longrightarrow c,
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{r_n}\longrightarrow c
\]
hold?

Finally, write
\[
 W_{n,B_n}
 =
 \operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)
\]
for the worst integrated radius computed with the third block in \(B_n\). Do there exist a fixed constant \(D>0\), a fixed \(\mathsf{amplitude}\) with \(0<\mathsf{amplitude}\leq1/4\), and sequences
\[
 P_0,P_{\mathrm{reg}},P_{\mathrm{loc}}:\mathbb N\to\mathcal M
\]
such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the laws \(P_0(n)\), \(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)\), and \(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)\) satisfy the declared clamp-model member conditions, their \(n\)-sample experiments satisfy independent observed-unit sampling, the pair \((P_0(n),P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n))\) satisfies the declared global Bernoulli shift at scale \(n^{-1/2}\), the pair \((P_0(n),P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n))\) satisfies the declared localized Bernoulli perturbation at \(\beta\), \(\delta_n\),
\[
 h_n=\operatorname{infoBandwidth}(n,\delta_n,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta),
\]
and \(\mathsf{amplitude}\), and
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)^{\otimes n}\middle\Vert P_0(n)^{\otimes n}\right)\leq D,
 \qquad
 \chi^2\!\left(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)^{\otimes n}\middle\Vert P_0(n)^{\otimes n}\right)\leq D?
\]
For these witnesses define
\[
 \Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}
 =
 \left|\theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)\right)-
          \theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_0(n)\right)\right|
  +
 \left|\theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)\right)-
          \theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_0(n)\right)\right|.
\]
Do the three matching limits
\[
 \frac{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{2W_{n,B_n}}{L_n^\star}\longrightarrow1
\]
hold? Here \(W_{n,B_n}\) is a radius, so \(2W_{n,B_n}\) is the candidate untruncated expected full length. The convention
\[
 \operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)=0
\]
when the affine feasible set is empty remains in force. The honesty, nondegeneracy, and optimality of the zero-totalized candidate are separate unresolved issues.

83e8210a27f5e28946c4ebcaaeaacdf7bd9c0213.title: Causal frontier lift
83e8210a27f5e28946c4ebcaaeaacdf7bd9c0213.body:
Let \(J\) be a positive integer, and let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The constants satisfy
\[
\beta>0,\qquad \kappa\geq0,\qquad L>0,\qquad c_->0,\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,
\]
\[
p_{\min}>0,\qquad p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad 0<\alpha<\frac12 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} The deterministic thresholds \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) satisfy
\[
0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta
\]
for every \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Split blocks.)} For each \(n\), \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is a deterministic three-way split with pairwise disjoint blocks and
\[
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{0,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{1,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{2,n}|.
\]
\end{itemize}
Let \(h_n\), the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\), be as in \cref{obj:def:bandwidth}, and let
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
be the frontier rate from \cref{obj:def:frontier}. Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\), with \(0<c<C\), depending only on the displayed regime constants, such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}, formed with split \(B_n\), order \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), bandwidth \(h_n\), and threshold \(\delta_n\), is observed-sample measurable, and the corresponding stabilized bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\), formed with the same split, order, bandwidth, and threshold, is an observed-sample measurable interval.

For the causal minimax criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) in \cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria}, the same \(n\) also satisfies
\[
c r_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_n-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|
\leq C r_n,
\]
\[
\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in \mathrm{CI}_n\}
\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
\[
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)
\leq C r_n,
\]
and, in the extended nonnegative-real order,
\[
\operatorname{ofReal}(c r_n)\leq L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
\leq \operatorname{ofReal}(C r_n).
\]

0d8baa9fc284375f650935cbf55c12b196f490ee.title: Observed law class \(\mathcal M\)
0d8baa9fc284375f650935cbf55c12b196f490ee.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])\), let
\[
p_x=P(X=x),\qquad x\in\mathcal X .
\]
The observed law class \(\mathcal M\) is
\[
\mathcal M
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])
:
P\text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning,obj:ass:holder-regression}
\right\}.
\]

14b83a4d81fdf9835ff1e0a16975fd2be8f819a0.title: Phase boundary regimes
14b83a4d81fdf9835ff1e0a16975fd2be8f819a0.body:
Let \(J\) be a positive integer and let
\[
\beta>0,\qquad
\kappa\geq 0,\qquad
L>0,\qquad
0<c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\qquad
0<p_{\min}\leq 1/J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad
0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
Define the phase and edge scales by
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}
=
n^{-1/\{2(\beta\kappa+2\beta+\kappa+1)\}},
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}
=
n^{-1/(2\beta+\kappa+1)} .
\]
Then
\[
\frac{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}{\delta_{\mathrm{edge},n}}\to\infty .
\]
Moreover, for every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq 1}\) with \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\), let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth in \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), and set
\[
a_n=\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta,
\qquad
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
as in \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\). The following conclusions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Regular thresholds.} If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to 0\), then \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\).
\item \textbf{Critical thresholds.} For every \(c_0>0\), if \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to c_0\), then \(a_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\) and \(r_n\asymp n^{-1/2}\).
\item \textbf{Vanishing atom-dominated thresholds.} If \(\delta_n/\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}\to\infty\) and \(\delta_n\to0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp
\delta_n^{\kappa+1}\bigl(n\delta_n^\kappa\bigr)^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)} .
\]
\item \textbf{Fixed thresholds.} For every \(\delta_0\in(0,\bar\delta]\), if \(\delta_n\to\delta_0\), then
\[
r_n\asymp n^{-\beta/(2\beta+1)} .
\]
\item \textbf{Zero threshold identities.} For every \(n\) and every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\),
\[
q_x(0)=0\quad\text{for every }x,\qquad
\theta_0(P)=\int Y\,dP,\qquad
r_n\big|_{\delta_n=0}=n^{-1/2},
\]
where the last identity uses the bandwidth \(h_n\) at threshold \(0\).
\item \textbf{Zero threshold estimator.} For every \(n\), every \(P\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), and every admissible three-way split \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\), the total-Gram estimator in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\), formed at threshold \(0\) with bandwidth \(h_n\), agrees under the product sampling law generated by \(P\) with
\[
z\mapsto
\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}\!\left(\frac{1}{|I_0|}\sum_{i\in I_0}Y_i\right).
\]
\item \textbf{Zero threshold stabilized guarantees.} For every deterministic sequence \(B_\bullet=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks, the stabilized zero-threshold procedure has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) for all sufficiently large \(n\). Its stabilized worst-case risk at threshold \(0\) and its stabilized worst-case expected length at threshold \(0\) with noncoverage level \(\alpha\) are both asymptotic to \(n^{-1/2}\).
\end{itemize}

db9bf8cfb671fc37faea94f49fb5e4bd09fa23ca.title: Exact-modulus handles \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) and \(\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n\)
db9bf8cfb671fc37faea94f49fb5e4bd09fa23ca.body:
With notation as in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation,obj:def:model-class}\), define
\[
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t)
=
\int \operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes n})(z).
\]
Here \(P\in\mathcal M\), \(I_2\) is a split block, \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(h_n>0\), \(t\geq0\), and the inputs \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\) are the corresponding member conditions imposed through \(P\in\mathcal M\).

For a realized design \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), set
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
The affine weight set is
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=
\left\{
w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}:
w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\quad
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
If \(V_{z,x}\) is the matrix whose row indexed by \(i\in S_{z,x}\) is \(v_\ell(u_i)^\top\), then the same affine constraints are
\[
V_{z,x}^\top w_{S_{z,x}}=e_0,
\qquad
G_x=V_{z,x}^\top V_{z,x}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) that are continuous and satisfy
\[
\left|f(a')-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}f^{(j)}(a)(a'-a)^j/j!\right|
\leq
L|a'-a|^\beta
\]
for every \(a,a'\in[0,1]\), where the derivatives are the intrinsic derivatives on \([0,1]\) used in the declared Hölder condition. For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define
\[
