\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
=
\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)
\right|
\]
and
\[
\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w)
=
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
+
t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
The realized exact modulus is
\[
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)
=
\begin{cases}
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}\mathcal Q_{z,x,t}(w),& \mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\
0,& \mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
The zero value on \(\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing\) is the real-valued totalization convention for singular realized designs.

Finally, set
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2},
\]
and define the worst integrated exact-modulus radius by
\[
\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t_\alpha)
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}(P,I_2,x,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta_n,h_n,t_\alpha).
\]
Both \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) and \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) are radius, or half-length, quantities. An untruncated symmetric interval with such a radius has full length twice the radius.

2ff02136694e2804743589a397400b4b8686f20f.title: Observed law class \(\mathcal M\)
2ff02136694e2804743589a397400b4b8686f20f.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])\), let
\[
p_x=P(X=x),
\qquad x\in\mathcal X .
\]
The observed-data law class \(\mathcal M\) is
\[
\mathcal M
=
\left\{
P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])
:
P\text{ satisfies the conditions listed below}
\right\}.
\]
Membership means that \(P\) satisfies:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Conditional density.)} The conditional-density condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law}\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum mass.)} The stratum-mass condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:stratum-mass}\).
\item \textbf{(Polynomial thinning.)} The polynomial-thinning condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}\).
\item \textbf{(Hölder regression.)} The Hölder member condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:holder-regression}\).
\end{itemize}

f75dd36c802ac8579fb0d1b3e2c85cc3ac66032f.title: Information-balance bandwidth \(h_n\)
f75dd36c802ac8579fb0d1b3e2c85cc3ac66032f.body:
The information-balance bandwidth \(h_n\) for the threshold sequence \(\delta_n\) is
\[
h_n
=
\inf\left\{
h\in(0,1-\bar\delta]:
n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h)^\kappa\geq 1
\right\},
\]
with \(h_n=1-\bar\delta\) when the displayed set is empty.

ecd405ec745440589fe8ae02fca05ad4eeb7d303.title: Local design quantities \(U_i,G_x,\Omega_x,w_{ix}\)
ecd405ec745440589fe8ae02fca05ad4eeb7d303.body:
For a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), the bandwidth \(h_n\) from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), a deterministic third split block \(I_2\), and a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), define
\[
U_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)^\top .
\]
The local count and total Gram matrix are
\[
N_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\},
\]
\[
G_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}
v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top .
\]
Let
\[
M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}
=
\frac{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
\]
and
\[
\lambda_\star
=
\frac{c_-}{c_+}\inf_{\rho\geq0}
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\right).
\]
The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) is
\[
\Omega_x
=
\left\{
N_x>0
\ \text{and}\
v^\top G_xv\geq\frac{\lambda_\star N_x}{2}\lVert v\rVert_2^2
\ \text{for every }v
\right\}.
\]
The exact local-polynomial intercept weight is
\[
w_{ix}
=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}\,
e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i),& \Omega_x,\\
0,& \Omega_x^{c}.
\end{cases}
\]

fec0cc79397d83e2b152df88b86f1d1698b96f1d.title: Full-data causal class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\)
fec0cc79397d83e2b152df88b86f1d1698b96f1d.body:
\(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) is the collection of full-data law packages \(P^{\mathrm F}\) satisfying the following memberwise structure relative to \(\cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:exchangeability,obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity}\).
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Latent response space.)} Each member carries its own standard Borel latent-response space \(\mathcal U\) and an \(\mathcal U\)-valued random variable \(U\).
\item \textbf{(Structural response maps.)} Each member carries jointly Borel maps
\[
g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1],
\qquad x\in\mathcal X,
\]
and a jointly measurable potential-outcome process
\[
\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Full-data law.)} Each member carries a probability law for
\[
(X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\}).
\]
\item \textbf{(Observed margin.)} The \((X,A,Y)\)-margin is some \(P\in\mathcal M\).
\item \textbf{(Causal member conditions.)} Within the member's own carrier, the simultaneous latent-response consistency, latent randomization, and fiberwise structural-mean continuity on \([0,\bar\delta]\) conditions hold.
\end{itemize}
The class is formed member by member, with membership determined on each member's own standard Borel carrier.

d563aaec17dc294f5f4b5f57630d37cc4b0d8885.title: Bandwidth balance root
d563aaec17dc294f5f4b5f57630d37cc4b0d8885.body:
Let \(h_n\) denote the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\) formed with \(\delta_n,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Smoothness exponent.)} \(\beta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Thinning exponent.)} \(\kappa\geq0\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold cap.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) is a deterministic real sequence satisfying \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
0<h_n,\qquad
h_n\leq 1-\bar\delta,\qquad
n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=1.
\]

292766a01c22741bfd5970b50cf942172219f77f.title: Good Gram weights
292766a01c22741bfd5970b50cf942172219f77f.body:
Fix \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), a split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) with pairwise disjoint blocks satisfying \(|I_r|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(r=0,1,2\), an observed sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), and a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Let \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\in\mathbb R\).  Suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive bandwidth.)} \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Positive population Gram constant.)} The constant \(\lambda_\star\) from \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\) satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Good local design.)} The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) from \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\) holds for \(B_n,z,x,\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\).
\end{itemize}
Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) and rescaled coordinates \(U_i\) from \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\) satisfy, for every \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix} U_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}.
\]
They also obey the two deterministic weight bounds
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}|w_{ix}|
\le
\frac{2\sqrt{\ell+1}}{\lambda_\star},
\]
and, with \(N_x\) denoting the local count in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_{ix}^2
\le
\frac{4(\ell+1)}{\lambda_\star^2 N_x}.
\]

00a9bc9bcb4dee17eedcdd91e41c825e52ad9623.title: Local Gram coercivity
00a9bc9bcb4dee17eedcdd91e41c825e52ad9623.body:
Fix an observed law \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), with constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+\), and \(p_{\min}\).  Let \(\ell\ge 0\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} \(\kappa\ge0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_+>0\), and \(p_{\min}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Local window.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\delta\ge0\), \(h>0\), and \(\delta+h\le1\).
\end{itemize}
For an observation \(O=(X,A,Y)\), set
\[
p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}(\delta,h)
=
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{X=x,\ 0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\right],
\]
and, for \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\), define the local monomial feature
\[
\phi_j(O)
=
\mathbf 1\!\left\{0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\left(\frac{A-\delta}{h}\right)^j .
\]
Then, with \(\lambda_\star\) denoting the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant from \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\), every \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\) satisfies
\[
\lambda_\star\,p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}(\delta,h)\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}v_j^2
\le
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}\sum_{k=0}^{\ell}
v_jv_k\,
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{X=x,\ 0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\phi_j(O)\phi_k(O)
\right].
\]

61bdcb74bb5cdf2417c4b5c679eee906c4152e10.title: Balanced weight energy bound
61bdcb74bb5cdf2417c4b5c679eee906c4152e10.body:
Let \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\) be an observed-data law on \(J\) strata, let \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) be a deterministic split, and fix a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P^{\otimes n}\) denote the canonical product sampling law of \(n\) observed units from \(P\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model and sampling.)} \(P\in\mathcal M(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), the observed sample is independently drawn from \(P\) as in \(\cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}\), and \(B_n\) is a three-way split as in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\).
\item \textbf{(Numerical conditions.)} \(n\ge 8\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\ge0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_+\ge0\), \(p_{\min}>0\), and \(\delta\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and design.)} \(h>0\), \(\delta+h\le1\), and the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\) satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Balance.)} The bandwidth is information-balanced:
\[
n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa=1.
\]
\end{itemize}
For the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\),
\[
\int
\left(\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix}(z)^2\right)^{1/2}
\,dP^{\otimes n}(z)
\le
\left(
\frac{336\{4(\ell+1)/\lambda_\star^2\}}
{p_{\min}c_-/(2\cdot 2^\kappa)}
\right)^{1/2}
h^\beta .
\]

994d3ce42e262f45f6aa9634cbec5a81b91a0772.title: Stabilized interval honesty
994d3ce42e262f45f6aa9634cbec5a81b91a0772.body:
Fix integers \(J\) and \(n\), deterministic split blocks \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\), constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\), and a threshold \(\delta\).  Let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth from \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\) evaluated at \((n,\delta,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta)\), and let \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) be the stabilized interval from \(\cref{obj:def:honest-interval}\) formed with split \(B\), bandwidth \(h_n\), and threshold \(\delta\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Split blocks.)} \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) consists of three deterministic, pairwise-disjoint subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with
\[
|I_0|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor,\qquad
|I_1|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor,\qquad
|I_2|\ge \lfloor n/4\rfloor .
\]
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The declared constants satisfy
\[
J\ge 1,\quad
\beta>0,\quad
\kappa\ge 0,\quad
L>0,\quad
0<c_-\le \kappa+1\le c_+,\quad
0<p_{\min}\le 1/J,\quad
0<\bar\delta<1,\quad
0<\alpha<1/2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\ge 4\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold range.)} \(\delta\in[0,\bar\delta]\).
\item \textbf{(Interior bandwidth.)} \(0<h_n\) and \(\delta+h_n\le 1\).
\end{itemize}
Then \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) is an observed-sample measurable interval, and for every observed-data law \(P\) in the clamp model \(\mathcal M\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
P^{\otimes n}\!\left\{
\theta_\delta(P)\in \mathrm{CI}_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)
\right\},
\]
where \(\theta_\delta(P)\) is the unsmoothed observed-data clamp target from \(\cref{obj:def:clamp-functional}\).

cafece80684004772c745dec6ec646dbe9ceefa0.title: Stabilized risk upper bound
cafece80684004772c745dec6ec646dbe9ceefa0.body:
Assume that the declared constants satisfy
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Strata.)} \(J\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness and thinning.)} \(\beta>0\) and \(\kappa\geq 0\).
\item \textbf{(Model radii.)} \(L>0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+\), and \(p_{\min}>0\) with \(p_{\min}\leq 1/J\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and calibration.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).
\end{itemize}
Then there is a constant \(C_{\mathrm{up}}>0\), depending on these declared constants, such that the following holds.  For every deterministic threshold sequence \((\delta_n)_{n\geq 1}\) with \(0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta\) for every \(n\), and for every deterministic split sequence \(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq 1}\) in which each \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) consists of pairwise disjoint subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with
\[
|I_{0,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor,\qquad
|I_{1,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor,\qquad
|I_{2,n}|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor,
\]
there is \(N<\infty\) such that, for every \(n\geq N\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|
\leq
C_{\mathrm{up}}\left(n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta\right),
\]
where \(\mathcal M\) is the model class in \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\), \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) is the clamp target in \(\cref{obj:def:clamp-functional}\), \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}\) is the total-Gram estimator in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\), \(h_n\) is the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\) in \(\cref{obj:def:bandwidth}\), and the rate is the frontier in \(\cref{obj:def:frontier}\).

bf9e9e3db3959ba6135a217c04b6d0b17aeeb3a4.title: Eventual bandwidth balance
bf9e9e3db3959ba6135a217c04b6d0b17aeeb3a4.body:
Let \(h_n\) denote the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} formed with \(\delta_n,\beta,\kappa,\bar\delta\). Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Hölder exponent.)} The exponent \(\beta\) appearing in \cref{obj:ass:holder-regression} satisfies \(\beta>0\).
\item \textbf{(Polynomial-thinning exponent.)} The exponent \(\kappa\) appearing in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} satisfies \(\kappa\geq0\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold cap.)} \(0<\bar\delta<1\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} \((\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) is a deterministic real sequence satisfying \(\delta_n\in[0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(n\).
\end{itemize}
Then, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
0<h_n,\qquad
h_n\leq 1-\bar\delta,\qquad
n h_n^{2\beta+1}(\delta_n+h_n)^\kappa=1.
\]

c26d20c7afe02c118d8f72ca6fa023a1bd7eaedb.title: Local Gram coercivity
c26d20c7afe02c118d8f72ca6fa023a1bd7eaedb.body:
Fix an observed law \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with conditional-density, stratum-mass, and polynomial-thinning components as in \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.  Fix constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+\), and \(p_{\min}\), and a degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).  Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Design constants.)} \(\kappa\ge0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_+>0\), and \(p_{\min}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Local window.)} \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\delta\ge0\), \(h>0\), and \(\delta+h\le1\).
\end{itemize}
For an observation \(O=(X,A,Y)\), set
\[
p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}(\delta,h)
=
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{X=x,\ 0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\right],
\]
and, for \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\), define the local monomial feature
\[
\phi_j(O)
=
\mathbf 1\!\left\{0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\left(\frac{A-\delta}{h}\right)^j .
\]
Then, with \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) denoting the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, every \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\) satisfies
\[
\lambda_\star\,p_x^{\mathrm{loc}}(\delta,h)\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}v_j^2
\le
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}\sum_{k=0}^{\ell}
v_jv_k\,
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf 1\!\left\{X=x,\ 0\le \frac{A-\delta}{h}\le 1\right\}
\phi_j(O)\phi_k(O)
\right].
\]

9da8c25c06d77279ee9c03ed869b5121970e4887.title: Balanced weight energy
9da8c25c06d77279ee9c03ed869b5121970e4887.body:
Let \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\) be an observed-data law on \(J\) strata, let \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) be a deterministic split, and fix a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and let \(P^{\otimes n}\) denote the canonical product sampling law of \(n\) observed units from \(P\).  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model and sampling.)} \(P\in\mathcal M(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with the polynomial-thinning, stratum-mass, and Hölder-regression components in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:holder-regression}; the observed sample is independently drawn from \(P\) as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}; and \(B_n\) is a three-way split as in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}.
\item \textbf{(Numerical conditions.)} \(n\ge 8\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\ge0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_+\ge0\), \(p_{\min}>0\), and \(\delta\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and design.)} \(h>0\), \(\delta+h\le1\), and the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Balance.)} The bandwidth is information-balanced:
\[
n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa=1.
\]
\end{itemize}
For the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation},
\[
\int
\left(\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix}(z)^2\right)^{1/2}
\,dP^{\otimes n}(z)
\le
\left(
\frac{336\{4(\ell+1)/\lambda_\star^2\}}
{p_{\min}c_-/(2\cdot 2^\kappa)}
\right)^{1/2}
h^\beta .
\]

7f9ed690c51d4f5a8c4b9e4e5df8060209e8fefa.title: Balanced weight energy
7f9ed690c51d4f5a8c4b9e4e5df8060209e8fefa.body:
Let \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), let \(P\) be an observed-data law on \(J\) strata, let \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) be a deterministic split, and fix a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).  Let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and define the observed product sampling law by
\[
P^{\otimes n}=\bigotimes_{j=1}^n P .
\]
Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Model and sampling.)} \(P\) belongs to the observed model class \(\mathcal M\) in \cref{obj:def:model-class} with fixed constants \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\), including the polynomial-thinning, stratum-mass, and Hölder-regression components in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:holder-regression}; the observed sample is independently drawn from \(P\) as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}; and \(B_n\) is a three-way split as in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}.
\item \textbf{(Numerical conditions.)} \(n\ge 8\), \(\beta>0\), \(\kappa\ge0\), \(c_->0\), \(c_+\ge0\), \(p_{\min}>0\), and \(\delta\ge0\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and design.)} \(h>0\), \(\delta+h\le1\), and the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation} satisfies \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Balance.)} The bandwidth is information-balanced:
\[
n h^{2\beta+1}(\delta+h)^\kappa=1.
\]
\end{itemize}
For the exact local-polynomial intercept weights \(w_{ix}\) from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation},
\[
\int
\left(\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix}(z)^2\right)^{1/2}
\,dP^{\otimes n}(z)
\le
\left(
\frac{336\{4(\ell+1)/\lambda_\star^2\}}
{p_{\min}c_-/(2\cdot 2^\kappa)}
\right)^{1/2}
h^\beta .
\]

8ad8c5fe00a4d4fdfb210c025b3a035e51481385.title: Power window lower bound
8ad8c5fe00a4d4fdfb210c025b3a035e51481385.body:
Let \(\delta\) be a threshold, \(h\) a window width, and \(\kappa\) a thinning exponent. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Threshold.)} \(0\le \delta\).
\item \textbf{(Window width.)} \(0<h\).
\item \textbf{(Exponent.)} \(0\le \kappa\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\frac{h}{2}\left(\frac{\delta+h}{2}\right)^{\kappa}
\le
\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h} a^{\kappa}\,da .
\]

8baf0b5119e097392814cd76966fc4ef79531a18.title: Positive Gram constant
8baf0b5119e097392814cd76966fc4ef79531a18.body:
In the local-design notation of \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, suppose:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} The polynomial degree is \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Thinning exponent.)} The exponent satisfies \(\kappa\ge 0\), as in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.
\item \textbf{(Envelope constants.)} The envelope constants satisfy \(c_->0\) and \(c_+>0\).
\end{itemize}
Then the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant
\[
\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)
=
\frac{c_-}{c_+}\inf_{\rho\ge 0}\lambda_{\min}(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho})
\]
is strictly positive:
\[
\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)>0.
\]

913116c02d1246c57a24dd17a9050c09323b959f.title: Uniform shifted coercivity
913116c02d1246c57a24dd17a9050c09323b959f.body:
Fix a polynomial degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\) and a thinning exponent \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\) with \(\kappa\ge 0\).  For the normalized reference moment matrix \(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\), there exists a constant \(c=c(\ell,\kappa)>0\) such that, for every shift \(\rho\ge 0\) and every vector \(z=(z_0,\ldots,z_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\),
\[
c\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} z_j^2
\le
z^\top M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}z .
\]

3d87bca270e6c410a4cdaf4495b98330305757c6.title: Local window mass
3d87bca270e6c410a4cdaf4495b98330305757c6.body:
Let \(P\), an observed-data law, belong to the model class \(\mathcal M\) of \(\cref{obj:def:model-class}\) with constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\).  Fix a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), a threshold \(\delta\in\mathbb R\), and a window width \(h\in\mathbb R\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive width.)} \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window support.)} \([\delta,\delta+h]\subseteq[0,1]\).
\end{itemize}
Then the population mass of the local window in stratum \(x\) is
\[
\int \mathbf 1\{X=x,\ 0\le (A-\delta)/h\le 1\}\,dP
=
p_x\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}\pi_x(a)\,da.
\]

f19a88fd579eaf2d43c69f17954c61190c03bcc6.title: Local Gram integral
f19a88fd579eaf2d43c69f17954c61190c03bcc6.body:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) as in \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with declared constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\).  Let \(x\in\mathcal X\), let \(\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and let \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Constant signs.)} \(\kappa\ge 0\), \(c_+\ge 0\), and \(p_{\min}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window.)} \(h>0\) and \([\delta,\delta+h]\subseteq[0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Entries.)} \(j,k\in\{0,\ldots,\ell\}\).
\end{itemize}
For \(u_\delta(a)=(a-\delta)/h\), write \(v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)\) as in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, and define the local feature
\[
\phi_j(O)=\mathbf 1\{0\le u_\delta(A)\le 1\}\,v_\ell(u_\delta(A))_j .
\]
Then the \((j,k)\) entry of the population localized Gram form satisfies
\[
\int \mathbf 1\{X=x,\ 0\le u_\delta(A)\le 1\}\,\phi_j(O)\phi_k(O)\,dP(O)
=
p_x\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}
\pi_x(a)\,
v_\ell(u_\delta(a))_j\,
v_\ell(u_\delta(a))_k\,da .
\]

d8d25f28e87799d1cb241b31c81694f79f5c2d2e.title: Scaled window coercivity
d8d25f28e87799d1cb241b31c81694f79f5c2d2e.body:
Let \(\ell\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) be the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant from \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Shape constants.)} \(\kappa\ge 0\), \(c_->0\), and \(c_+>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window.)} \(\delta\ge 0\) and \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient vector.)} \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\lambda_\star c_+
\left(\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h} a^\kappa\,\mathrm da\right)
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} v_j^2
\le
c_-
\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}
\left\{
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}
v_j\left(\frac{a-\delta}{h}\right)^j
\right\}^2
a^\kappa\,\mathrm da .
\]

54afef69c6347b646651549a8e66bd761fb4624e.title: Good Gram reproduction
54afef69c6347b646651549a8e66bd761fb4624e.body:
Fix \(J,n,\ell\in\mathbb N\), a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and deterministic split blocks \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\).  Use the local-design notation \(U_i\), \(N_x\), \(G_x\), \(\lambda_\star\), \(\Omega_x\), and \(w_{ix}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\).

Assume that \(\lambda_\star>0\) and that the good-design event \(\Omega_x\) holds for \(B_n,z,x,\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\).  Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weights reproduce every monomial coordinate at the threshold: for every \(j=0,\ldots,\ell\),
\[
\sum_{i\in I_2} w_{ix} U_i^j
=
\begin{cases}
1, & j=0,\\
0, & j\ne 0.
\end{cases}
\]

217aaeed34c35cecfdc62db8751d888aa0b002b5.title: Intercept weight formula
217aaeed34c35cecfdc62db8751d888aa0b002b5.body:
Fix the local-design notation of \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\) and the split-block construction of \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\).  Let \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) be a deterministic three-way split with pairwise disjoint blocks, each of cardinality at least \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\).  Fix a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), a degree \(\ell\), constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+\), a threshold \(\delta\), a window width \(h\), and an index \(i\).

Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Good design.)} The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) holds for \(B_n,z,x,\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\).
\item \textbf{(Regression block.)} The index satisfies \(i\in I_2\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum match.)} The realized stratum satisfies \(X_i=x\).
\item \textbf{(Local window.)} With \(U_i=(A_i-\delta)/h\), one has \(U_i\in[0,1]\).
\end{itemize}

Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weight satisfies
\[
w_{ix}=e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i).
\]

7aab13e51636befd508cb611c53108739a8e5e36.title: Pointwise intercept-weight bound
7aab13e51636befd508cb611c53108739a8e5e36.body:
Fix integers \(J,n,\ell\), a split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\), a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), constants \(\kappa,c_-,c_+,\delta,h\in\mathbb R\), and an index \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\).  With \(N_x\), \(\lambda_\star\), \(\Omega_x\), and \(w_{ix}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\), assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Split.)} The split \(B_n\) has three pairwise disjoint deterministic blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\), each of cardinality at least \(\lfloor n/4\rfloor\), as in \(\cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}\).
\item \textbf{(Positive population Gram constant.)} \(\lambda_\star>0\).
\item \textbf{(Good design.)} The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) holds at the realized sample \(z\).
\end{itemize}
Then the exact local-polynomial intercept weight at index \(i\) satisfies
\[
|w_{ix}|
\le
\left(\frac{\lambda_\star N_x}{2}\right)^{-1}\sqrt{\ell+1}.
\]

57dd96f53ec36cc45fbeb302208d0e101f51e209.title: Power window integral lower bound
57dd96f53ec36cc45fbeb302208d0e101f51e209.body:
Using the thinning-exponent notation of \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}, let \(\delta\) be a threshold, \(h\) a window width, and \(\kappa\) an exponent. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Threshold.)} \(0\le \delta\).
\item \textbf{(Window width.)} \(0<h\).
\item \textbf{(Exponent.)} \(0\le \kappa\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\frac{h}{2}\left(\frac{\delta+h}{2}\right)^{\kappa}
\le
\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h} a^{\kappa}\,da .
\]

73bcb4092cd67bb1305c8201d84e7006a51f60e0.title: Uniform shifted moment coercivity
73bcb4092cd67bb1305c8201d84e7006a51f60e0.body:
Fix a polynomial degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\) and a thinning exponent \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\) satisfying the nonnegativity condition in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.  For the normalized reference moment matrix \(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\) in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, there exists a constant \(c=c(\ell,\kappa)>0\) such that, for every shift \(\rho\ge 0\) and every vector \(z=(z_0,\ldots,z_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\),
\[
c\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} z_j^2
\le
z^\top M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}z .
\]

83f6587ff8788b144d6b18b39e37cd415c1922a1.title: Local window mass identity
83f6587ff8788b144d6b18b39e37cd415c1922a1.body:
Let \(P\), an observed-data law, belong to the model class \(\mathcal M\) of \cref{obj:def:model-class}, with conditional treatment densities, stratum masses, and polynomial thinning as in \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} for constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\).  Fix:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Stratum.)} A stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\).
\item \textbf{(Threshold and width.)} A threshold \(\delta\in\mathbb R\) and a window width \(h\in\mathbb R\) with \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window support.)} \([\delta,\delta+h]\subseteq[0,1]\).
\end{itemize}
Then the population mass of the local window in stratum \(x\) is
\[
\int \mathbf 1\{X=x,\ 0\le (A-\delta)/h\le 1\}\,dP
=
p_x\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}\pi_x(a)\,da.
\]

532c051adc7d8398db2710686ef5569ed93d78f2.title: Local Gram integral identity
532c051adc7d8398db2710686ef5569ed93d78f2.body:
Fix a law \(P\in\mathcal M\) with declared constants \((\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min})\), as in \cref{obj:def:model-class,obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.  Let \(\ell\in\mathbb N\), \(x\in\mathcal X\), and \(\delta,h\in\mathbb R\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Constant signs.)} \(\kappa\ge 0\), \(c_+\ge 0\), and \(p_{\min}>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window.)} \(h>0\) and \([\delta,\delta+h]\subseteq[0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Entries.)} \(j,k\in\{0,\ldots,\ell\}\).
\end{itemize}
For \(u_\delta(a)=(a-\delta)/h\), write \(v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)\) as in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, and define
\[
\phi_j(O)=\mathbf 1\{0\le u_\delta(A)\le 1\}\,v_\ell(u_\delta(A))_j .
\]
Then
\[
\int \mathbf 1\{X=x,\ 0\le u_\delta(A)\le 1\}\,\phi_j(O)\phi_k(O)\,dP(O)
=
p_x\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}
\pi_x(a)\,
v_\ell(u_\delta(a))_j\,
v_\ell(u_\delta(a))_k\,da .
\]

be431726fab8ab2c4c41f5b9890819bb19523ad1.title: Scaled window coercivity
be431726fab8ab2c4c41f5b9890819bb19523ad1.body:
Let \(\ell\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\lambda_\star=\lambda_\star(\ell,\kappa,c_-,c_+)\) be the uniform population Gram lower-bound constant from \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}, formed with the lower and upper thinning constants in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}. Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Shape constants.)} \(\kappa\ge 0\), \(c_->0\), and \(c_+>0\).
\item \textbf{(Window.)} \(\delta\ge 0\) and \(h>0\).
\item \textbf{(Coefficient vector.)} \(v=(v_0,\ldots,v_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\).
\end{itemize}
Then
\[
\lambda_\star c_+
\left(\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h} a^\kappa\,\mathrm da\right)
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} v_j^2
\le
c_-
\int_{\delta}^{\delta+h}
\left\{
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}
v_j\left(\frac{a-\delta}{h}\right)^j
\right\}^2
a^\kappa\,\mathrm da .
\]

0abb54dedf83a4cd31cbbadb5065313ac1f71eaf.title: Uniform shifted coercivity
0abb54dedf83a4cd31cbbadb5065313ac1f71eaf.body:
Fix objects satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} The polynomial degree is \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Exponent.)} The thinning exponent is \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative exponent.)} The exponent satisfies the nonnegative-exponent condition in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}, namely \(\kappa\ge 0\).
\item \textbf{(Reference moments.)} For each shift \(\rho\), \(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\) is the normalized reference moment matrix in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}.
\end{itemize}
There exists a constant \(c=c(\ell,\kappa)>0\) such that, for every \(\rho\ge 0\) and every \(z=(z_0,\ldots,z_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\),
\[
c\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} z_j^2
\le
z^\top M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}z .
\]
The same constant applies uniformly over all nonnegative shifts \(\rho\).

4c63de32138e457aa5c70ad5aacdd7e6e4016c25.title: Uniform shifted moment coercivity
4c63de32138e457aa5c70ad5aacdd7e6e4016c25.body:
Fix objects satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} The polynomial degree is \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Exponent.)} The thinning exponent is \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegative exponent.)} The exponent satisfies \(\cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}\).
\item \textbf{(Reference moments.)} For each shift \(\rho\), \(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\) is the normalized reference moment matrix in \(\cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}\).
\end{itemize}
There exists a constant \(c=c(\ell,\kappa)>0\) such that, for every \(\rho\ge 0\) and every \(z=(z_0,\ldots,z_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\),
\[
c\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} z_j^2
\le
z^\top M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}z .
\]
The same constant applies uniformly over all nonnegative shifts \(\rho\).

04ab5400ac2a9606a53d04754bb85af5be111707.title: Uniform shifted coercivity
04ab5400ac2a9606a53d04754bb85af5be111707.body:
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Degree.)} Fix a polynomial degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Exponent.)} Fix a thinning exponent \(\kappa\in\mathbb R\).
\item \textbf{(Nonnegativity.)} The exponent satisfies \(0\le \kappa\), as in \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning}.
\item \textbf{(Reference matrix.)} Let \(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\) denote the normalized population reference moment matrix in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation}.
\end{itemize}
Then there exists a constant \(c=c(\ell,\kappa)>0\) such that, for every shift \(\rho\ge 0\) and every vector \(z=(z_0,\ldots,z_\ell)\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\),
\[
c\sum_{j=0}^{\ell} z_j^2
\le
z^\top M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}z .
\]

1b720144105a3ae3f8fc7977b98a1e19f501890c.title: Local-polynomial degree
1b720144105a3ae3f8fc7977b98a1e19f501890c.body:
For each smoothness exponent \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), the local-polynomial degree is
\[
\ell(\beta):=\max\{\lceil\beta\rceil_{\mathbb N}-1,0\},
\]
where \(\lceil\beta\rceil_{\mathbb N}\) denotes the least natural number greater than or equal to \(\beta\).

60a36f3ea79bedd0997ade8c9a632c01c0ebb764.title: Exact modulus radius
60a36f3ea79bedd0997ade8c9a632c01c0ebb764.body:
With notation as in \cref{obj:def:local-design-notation,obj:def:model-class}, fix \(P\in\mathcal M\) under the displayed \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min}\) member conditions, a deterministic split \(B=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) with pairwise-disjoint blocks satisfying \(|I_m|\geq \lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(m=0,1,2\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), a local-polynomial degree \(\ell\in\mathbb N\), a threshold \(\delta\), a bandwidth \(h>0\), and a multiplier \(t\geq0\). For a realized observed sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), with \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), set
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta}{h},
\qquad
S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
The affine weight set is
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=
\left\{
w=(w_i)_{i=1}^n\in\mathbb R^n:
w_i=0\ \text{whenever } i\notin I_2\ \text{or }X_i\neq x\ \text{or }u_i\notin[0,1],
\quad
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), let \(B^{\mathrm H}_{z,x}(w)\) denote the exact Hölder bias term from the \((\beta,L)\)-Hölder regression class in \(\cref{obj:ass:holder-regression}\). Define the realized affine-modulus radius by
\[
R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t)
=
\inf\left\{
B^{\mathrm H}_{z,x}(w)
+
t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}
:
w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}
\right\},
\]
with the real-valued convention that this infimum is \(0\) when the displayed feasible set is empty. The integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
M^{\mathrm{ex}}_{x}(P,B,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta,h,t)
=
\int R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t)\,\mathrm dP^{\otimes n}(z),
\]
where \(P^{\otimes n}\) is the canonical product law of the observed sample. Both \(R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t)\) and \(M^{\mathrm{ex}}_{x}(P,B,\ell,\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\delta,h,t)\) are radius, or half-length, quantities.

fef9f1ce2a4af8aac74c1fbc808fd507bbf3a245.title: Causal frontier lift
fef9f1ce2a4af8aac74c1fbc808fd507bbf3a245.body:
Let \(J\in\mathbb N\), and let \(\beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regime constants.)} The constants satisfy
\[
0<J,\qquad
\beta>0,\qquad
\kappa\geq0,\qquad
L>0,\qquad
c_->0,\qquad
c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,
\]
\[
p_{\min}>0,\qquad
p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\qquad
0<\bar\delta<1,\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac12 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Threshold sequence.)} The deterministic thresholds \((\delta_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}\) satisfy
\[
0\leq \delta_n\leq \bar\delta
\]
for every \(n\in\mathbb N\).
\item \textbf{(Split blocks.)} For each \(n\in\mathbb N\), \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is a deterministic three-way split with pairwise disjoint blocks and
\[
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{0,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{1,n}|,\qquad
\left\lfloor \frac n4\right\rfloor\leq |I_{2,n}|.
\]
\end{itemize}
Let \(h_n\), the information-balance bandwidth for \(\delta_n\), be as in \cref{obj:def:bandwidth}, and let
\[
r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta
\]
be the frontier rate from \cref{obj:def:frontier}. Then there exist constants \(c,C\in\mathbb R\), with \(0<c<C\), depending only on these regime constants, such that, for every threshold sequence and every deterministic split-block sequence satisfying the preceding conditions, all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy the following conclusions.

The total-Gram estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) in \cref{obj:def:total-gram-estimator}, formed with split \(B_n\), order \(\ell=\lceil\beta\rceil-1\), bandwidth \(h_n\), and threshold \(\delta_n\), is observed-sample measurable. The corresponding bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) in \cref{obj:def:honest-interval}, formed with the same split, order, bandwidth, and threshold, is an observed-sample measurable interval.

For the causal minimax criteria \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) in \cref{obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria},
\[
c r_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
\leq
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}
\left|\widehat\theta_n-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\right|
\leq C r_n,
\]
\[
\inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in \mathrm{CI}_n\}
\geq 1-\alpha,
\]
\[
\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
\mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)
\leq C r_n.
\]
Moreover, in the extended nonnegative-real order, after embedding the nonnegative real bounds into \(\mathbb R_{\geq0}\cup\{\infty\}\),
\[
c r_n\leq L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\leq C r_n .
\]

07fc31ab8d1316cbc85ba582e52ab08e8deef890.title: Sharp length calibration
07fc31ab8d1316cbc85ba582e52ab08e8deef890.body:
The sharp constant question asks for the following property. For every
\[
 J\in\mathbb N,\qquad
 \beta,\kappa,L,c_-,c_+,p_{\min},\bar\delta,\alpha\in\mathbb R
\]
satisfying
\[
 J>0,\quad \beta>0,\quad \kappa\geq0,\quad L>0,\quad c_->0,\quad
 c_-\leq \kappa+1\leq c_+,\quad
 0<p_{\min}\leq \frac1J,\quad
 0<\bar\delta<1,\quad 0<\alpha<\frac12,
\]
there is a constant \(c>0\) such that every deterministic threshold sequence
\(\delta_{\bullet}=(\delta_n)_{n\geq1}\) with \(0\leq\delta_n\leq\bar\delta\) for all \(n\), and whose phase-boundary ratio satisfies either
\[
 \frac{\delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}\longrightarrow q
 \quad\text{for some }q\geq0
\]
or
\[
 \frac{\delta_n}{\delta_{\mathrm{crit},n}}\longrightarrow\infty,
\]
has the following simultaneous calibration properties. First,
\[
 \frac{L_n^\star}{r_n}\longrightarrow c,
 \qquad
 r_n=n^{-1/2}+\delta_n^{\kappa+1}h_n^\beta,
\]
where \(h_n\) is the information-balance bandwidth from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth} and \(r_n\) is the frontier from \cref{obj:def:frontier}. Second, there exists a deterministic sequence
\(B_{\bullet}=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) of admissible three-way split blocks such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M}
 P^{\otimes n}
 \left\{
   \theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
 \right\}
 \geq 1-\alpha,
\]
where \(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\) is the exact-modulus interval obtained from the split \(B_n\) using the exact-modulus construction of \cref{obj:def:exact-modulus-handle}. Its worst-case expected length satisfies
\[
 \frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{r_n}\longrightarrow c.
\]
Finally, the same sequence \(B_{\bullet}\) admits least-favorable mixed-experiment witnesses: there are a constant \(D>0\), an amplitude \(0<\mathsf{amplitude}\leq1/4\), and sequences
\[
 P_0,P_{\mathrm{reg}},P_{\mathrm{loc}}:\mathbb N\to\mathcal M
\]
such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), the three laws satisfy the clamp-model member conditions; their \(n\)-sample laws are the product laws in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling}; the pair \((P_0(n),P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n))\) has the declared global Bernoulli shift at scale \(n^{-1/2}\); the pair \((P_0(n),P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n))\) has the declared localized Bernoulli perturbation at \(\beta\), \(\delta_n\), \(h_n\), and \(\mathsf{amplitude}\); and
\[
 \chi^2\!\left(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)^{\otimes n}\middle\Vert P_0(n)^{\otimes n}\right)\leq D,
 \qquad
 \chi^2\!\left(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)^{\otimes n}\middle\Vert P_0(n)^{\otimes n}\right)\leq D.
\]
With
\[
 \Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}
 =
 \left|\theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_{\mathrm{reg}}(n)\right)-
          \theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_0(n)\right)\right|
  +
 \left|\theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_{\mathrm{loc}}(n)\right)-
          \theta_{\delta_n}\!\left(P_0(n)\right)\right|,
\]
and with \(W_{n,B_n}\) denoting the worst integrated exact-modulus radius from
\cref{obj:def:exact-modulus-handle} computed using the third block in \(B_n\), the matching limits are
\[
 \frac{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{mix}}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}}{2W_{n,B_n}}\longrightarrow1,
 \qquad
 \frac{2W_{n,B_n}}{L_n^\star}\longrightarrow1.
\]

9b374c1994f107f4645cf628f588321c5a0441b5.title: Hölder regression regularity
9b374c1994f107f4645cf628f588321c5a0441b5.body:
The regression function \(\mu_x^P\) satisfies the following condition with parameters \(\beta\) and \(L\). For every \(x\in\mathcal X\):
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Continuity.)} The map \(a\mapsto \mu_x^P(a)\) is continuous on \([0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Range.)} For every \(a\in[0,1]\), \(\mu_x^P(a)\in[0,1]\).
\item \textbf{(Regression version.)} The function \(\mu_X^P(A)\) realizes the conditional outcome regression given the complete design:
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X,A]=\mu_X^P(A)
\quad P\text{-almost surely}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Hölder Taylor remainder.)} Let \(\ell=\ell(\beta)\) be the local-polynomial order defined in \cref{obj:synth_19}. For all \(s,t\in[0,1]\), with derivatives taken intrinsically on \([0,1]\),
\[
\left|
\mu_x^P(t)
-
\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}
\frac{(\mu_x^P)^{(j)}(s)}{j!}(t-s)^j
\right|
\le
L|t-s|^\beta .
\]
\end{itemize}

78d16d21eb04bfbd8171e0244c1143eac0e06de4.title: Local design notation
78d16d21eb04bfbd8171e0244c1143eac0e06de4.body:
Let \(\ell=\ell(\beta)\), where \(\ell(\beta)\) is defined in \cref{obj:synth_19}. For a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), the bandwidth \(h_n\) from \cref{obj:def:bandwidth}, deterministic split blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\) as in \cref{obj:synth_8}, and a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), put
\[
U_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)^\top .
\]
Define
\[
N_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\},
\]
and
\[
G_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}
v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top .
\]
Let
\[
M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}
=
\frac{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
\]
and
\[
\lambda_\star
=
\frac{c_-}{c_+}\inf_{\rho\geq0}
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\right).
\]
The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) is
\[
\Omega_x
=
\left\{
N_x>0
\ \text{and}\
v^\top G_xv\geq\frac{\lambda_\star N_x}{2}\lVert v\rVert_2^2
\ \text{for every }v
\right\}.
\]
The exact local-polynomial intercept weight is
\[
w_{ix}
=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}\,
e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i),& \Omega_x,\\
0,& \Omega_x^{c}.
\end{cases}
\]

Use the notation and standing objects in \cref{obj:synth_1,obj:synth_2,obj:synth_3,obj:synth_4,obj:synth_5,obj:synth_6,obj:synth_11,obj:synth_8,obj:synth_10,obj:synth_12,obj:synth_13,obj:synth_14,obj:synth_15,obj:synth_16,obj:synth_17,obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:exchangeability,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning,obj:ass:holder-regression,obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity,obj:def:model-class,obj:def:clamp-policy,obj:def:clamp-functional,obj:def:bandwidth,obj:def:frontier,obj:def:local-design-notation,obj:def:total-gram-estimator,obj:def:honest-interval,obj:def:exact-modulus-handle,obj:def:full-data-model-class,obj:def:causal-clamp-mean,obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria,obj:def:continuity-model-class,obj:def:continuity-clamp-functional,obj:def:continuity-frontier,obj:def:continuity-fallback-estimator,obj:def:continuity-honest-interval,obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class,obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria,obj:prop:pushforward-setup,obj:prop:policy-support,obj:prop:causal-bridge,obj:lem:shifted-moment-coercivity,obj:lem:lambda-star-positive,obj:lem:power-window-integral-lower,obj:lem:local-window-mass,obj:lem:local-gram-entry-integral,obj:lem:scaled-window-coercivity,obj:lem:intercept-weight-formula,obj:lem:good-gram-reproduction,obj:lem:intercept-weight-pointwise,obj:thm:phase-diagram,obj:prop:one-cell-calibration,obj:oeq:sharp-constant,obj:prop:observed-margin-surjectivity,obj:lem:continuity-regression-extension-unique,obj:prop:continuity-causal-bridge,obj:prop:continuity-observed-margin-surjectivity,obj:thm:continuity-only-frontier,obj:lem:bandwidth-balance,obj:lem:local-gram-coercivity,obj:lem:good-gram-weights,obj:lem:weight-energy-balance,obj:lem:stabilized-interval-honesty,obj:lem:stabilized-risk-upper,obj:lem:bandwidth-phases,obj:lem:total-gram,obj:thm:minimax-risk,obj:thm:honest-length,obj:thm:causal-frontier-lift,obj:synth_19}. Let \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,J\}\), let \(O=(X,A,Y)\in\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]\), and let \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])\). Write
\[
p_x=P(X=x).
\]
Let \(\ell=\ell(\beta)\) be the local-polynomial degree defined in \cref{obj:synth_19}. The law \(P\) belongs to \(\mathcal M\) when, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the following conditions hold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Conditional density.)} For every Borel set \(B\subseteq[0,1]\),
\[
P(A\in B\mid X=x)=\int_B \pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da
\]
for a Borel density \(\pi_x\).
\item \textbf{(Stratum mass.)}
\[
p_x\ge p_{\min}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Polynomial thinning.)} For Lebesgue-almost every \(a\in[0,1]\),
\[
c_-a^\kappa\le \pi_x(a)\le c_+a^\kappa.
\]
\item \textbf{(Hölder regression.)} An almost-everywhere version of \(a\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) has a continuous extension \(\mu_x^P:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) such that, for all \(s,t\in[0,1]\),
\[
\left|\mu_x^P(t)-\sum_{j=0}^{\ell}\frac{(\mu_x^P)^{(j)}(s)}{j!}(t-s)^j\right|\le L|t-s|^\beta.
\]
\end{itemize}
The law \(P\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) when, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the conditional-density, stratum-mass, and polynomial-thinning conditions above hold, and an almost-everywhere version of \(a\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) has a unique continuous extension
\[
\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P:[0,\bar\delta]\to[0,1].
\]

b997c7714b38958c9aaa944c2e0f1d5c934a1f20.body:
For a realized sample \(z=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), deterministic split blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), local-polynomial degree \(\ell\), threshold \(\delta_n\), and bandwidth \(h_n\), put
\[
U_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)^\top .
\]
Define the local count by
\[
N_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ A_i\in[\delta_n,\delta_n+h_n]\}.
\]
Define the total local Gram matrix by
\[
G_x
=
\sum_{i\in I_2}
\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\}
v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top .
\]
For \(\rho\geq0\), define
\[
M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}
=
\frac{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du}
{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du},
\]
and set
\[
\lambda_\star
=
\frac{c_-}{c_+}
\inf_{\rho\geq0}
\lambda_{\min}\!\left(M_{\ell,\kappa,\rho}\right).
\]
The good-design event \(\Omega_x\) is the event that
\[
N_x>0
\]
and, for every vector \(v\in\mathbb R^{\ell+1}\),
\[
v^\top G_xv
\geq
\frac{\lambda_\star N_x}{2}\lVert v\rVert_2^2 .
\]

\[
K_{ix}
=
\mathbf 1\{i\in I_2,\ X_i=x,\ 0\leq U_i\leq1\},
\]

547f7a5e9d3fead9e39f522856223d957c693597.body:
Assume the notation, model conditions, and preceding constructions in \cref{obj:synth_1,obj:synth_2,obj:synth_3,obj:synth_4,obj:synth_5,obj:synth_6,obj:synth_11,obj:synth_8,obj:synth_10,obj:synth_12,obj:synth_13,obj:synth_14,obj:synth_15,obj:synth_16,obj:synth_17,obj:synth_18,obj:synth_19,obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:exchangeability,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning,obj:ass:holder-regression,obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity,obj:def:model-class,obj:def:clamp-policy,obj:def:clamp-functional,obj:def:bandwidth,obj:def:frontier,obj:def:local-design-notation,obj:def:total-gram-estimator,obj:def:honest-interval,obj:def:exact-modulus-handle,obj:def:full-data-model-class,obj:def:causal-clamp-mean,obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria,obj:def:continuity-model-class,obj:def:continuity-clamp-functional,obj:def:continuity-frontier,obj:def:continuity-fallback-estimator,obj:def:continuity-honest-interval,obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class,obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria,obj:prop:pushforward-setup,obj:prop:policy-support,obj:prop:causal-bridge,obj:lem:shifted-moment-coercivity,obj:lem:lambda-star-positive,obj:lem:power-window-integral-lower,obj:lem:local-window-mass,obj:lem:local-gram-entry-integral,obj:lem:scaled-window-coercivity,obj:lem:intercept-weight-formula,obj:lem:good-gram-reproduction,obj:lem:intercept-weight-pointwise,obj:thm:phase-diagram,obj:prop:one-cell-calibration,obj:oeq:sharp-constant,obj:prop:observed-margin-surjectivity,obj:lem:continuity-regression-extension-unique,obj:prop:continuity-causal-bridge,obj:prop:continuity-observed-margin-surjectivity,obj:thm:continuity-only-frontier,obj:lem:bandwidth-balance,obj:lem:local-gram-coercivity,obj:lem:good-gram-weights,obj:lem:weight-energy-balance,obj:lem:stabilized-interval-honesty,obj:lem:stabilized-risk-upper,obj:lem:bandwidth-phases,obj:lem:total-gram,obj:thm:minimax-risk,obj:thm:honest-length,obj:thm:causal-frontier-lift}. Fix an admissible deterministic three-way split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) at sample size \(n\). For a realized observed sample \(z\), let \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)\) be the total-Gram estimator formed with the blocks in \(B_n\), and evaluate the realized affine-modulus radius \(R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)\) on the \((X,A)\)-projection of \(z\) using the third block \(I_2\), where
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}.
\]
Define
\[
R_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t_\alpha).
\]
The exact-modulus interval is
\[
C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\left[
\max\left\{0,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)-R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\},
\min\left\{1,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)+R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\}
\right].
\]
Its worst-case expected length over the observed-data model is
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left[
\operatorname{len}\!\left(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right)
\right].
\]

\mathfrak W_n(t)

\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}

\]

d35aace5778e198cd9b4b4bb2356e7b0c97518a4.title: Exact-modulus radius \(W_{n,B_n}\)
d35aace5778e198cd9b4b4bb2356e7b0c97518a4.body:
Adopt the notation and hypotheses of \cref{obj:synth_1,obj:synth_2,obj:synth_3,obj:synth_4,obj:synth_5,obj:synth_6,obj:synth_11,obj:synth_8,obj:synth_10,obj:synth_12,obj:synth_13,obj:synth_14,obj:synth_16,obj:synth_17,obj:synth_18,obj:synth_19,obj:synth_20,obj:ass:iid-sampling,obj:ass:conditional-density-law,obj:ass:consistency,obj:ass:exchangeability,obj:ass:stratum-mass,obj:ass:polynomial-thinning,obj:ass:holder-regression,obj:ass:full-data-response-continuity,obj:def:model-class,obj:def:clamp-policy,obj:def:clamp-functional,obj:def:bandwidth,obj:def:frontier,obj:def:local-design-notation,obj:def:total-gram-estimator,obj:def:honest-interval,obj:def:exact-modulus-handle,obj:def:full-data-model-class,obj:def:causal-clamp-mean,obj:def:causal-frontier-criteria,obj:def:continuity-model-class,obj:def:continuity-clamp-functional,obj:def:continuity-frontier,obj:def:continuity-fallback-estimator,obj:def:continuity-honest-interval,obj:def:continuity-full-data-model-class,obj:def:continuity-frontier-criteria,obj:prop:pushforward-setup,obj:prop:policy-support,obj:prop:causal-bridge,obj:lem:shifted-moment-coercivity,obj:lem:lambda-star-positive,obj:lem:power-window-integral-lower,obj:lem:local-window-mass,obj:lem:local-gram-entry-integral,obj:lem:scaled-window-coercivity,obj:lem:intercept-weight-formula,obj:lem:good-gram-reproduction,obj:lem:intercept-weight-pointwise,obj:thm:phase-diagram,obj:prop:one-cell-calibration,obj:oeq:sharp-constant,obj:prop:observed-margin-surjectivity,obj:lem:continuity-regression-extension-unique,obj:prop:continuity-causal-bridge,obj:prop:continuity-observed-margin-surjectivity,obj:thm:continuity-only-frontier,obj:lem:bandwidth-balance,obj:lem:local-gram-coercivity,obj:lem:good-gram-weights,obj:lem:weight-energy-balance,obj:lem:stabilized-interval-honesty,obj:lem:stabilized-risk-upper,obj:lem:bandwidth-phases,obj:lem:total-gram,obj:thm:minimax-risk,obj:thm:honest-length,obj:thm:causal-frontier-lift}.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), a deterministic third split block \(I_2\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), and a multiplier \(t\geq0\).  For a realized design \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), set
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=
\left\{
w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}:
w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of continuous functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) satisfying the declared order-\(\ell\) Hölder Taylor-remainder bound with exponent \(\beta\) and radius \(L\).  For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define the realized Hölder bias functional
\[
B_{z,x}(w)
=
\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)
\right|.
\]
The realized affine-modulus radius at multiplier \(t\) is
\[
\mathcal R_{z,x}(t)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}
\left\{
B_{z,x}(w)
+
t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}
\right\},
&\mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\[1ex]
0,&\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
The integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,x}(P,I_2;t)
=
\int
\mathcal R_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes I_2})(z),
\]
where \(P_{X,A}^{\otimes I_2}\) is the independent observed-design product law on the coordinates in \(I_2\).

If \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is an admissible deterministic three-way split at sample size \(n\), its worst integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
W_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\mathfrak R_{n,x}\!\left(P,I_{2,n};t_\alpha\right),
\qquad
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}.
\]
Thus \(W_{n,B_n}\) is a radius quantity computed from the third block of \(B_n\), and the associated untruncated symmetric full length is \(2W_{n,B_n}\).

groups.title: Exact-modulus interval and worst-case expected length
groups.body:
Fix an admissible deterministic three-way split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) at sample size \(n\). For a realized observed sample \(z\), let \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)\) denote the total-Gram estimator formed with the blocks in \(B_n\), and evaluate \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)\) on the \((X,A)\)-projection of \(z\) using the third block \(I_2\), where \(t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}\). Define the realized exact-modulus radius
\[
R_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t_\alpha).
\]
The exact-modulus interval is the truncated symmetric interval
\[
C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\left[
\max\left\{0,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)-R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\},
\min\left\{1,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)+R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\}
\right].
\]
Its worst-case expected length over the observed-data model is
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left[
\operatorname{len}\!\left(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right)
\right].
\]

groups.title: Integrated exact-modulus radii
groups.body:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), a deterministic third split block \(I_2\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), and a multiplier \(t\geq0\).  For a realized design \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), set
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=\left\{w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}:
w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\quad
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of continuous functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) satisfying the declared order-\(\ell\) Hölder Taylor-remainder bound with exponent \(\beta\) and radius \(L\).  For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), put
\[
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
=
\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)\right|
\]
and
\[
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)
=
\begin{cases}
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}
\left\{
\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)
+t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}
\right\},
&\mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\
0,&\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
The integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,x}(P,I_2;t)
=
\int
\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes I_2})(z),
\]
where \(P_{X,A}^{\otimes I_2}\) is the independent observed-design law on the coordinates in \(I_2\).

If \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is an admissible deterministic three-way split at sample size \(n\), define its worst integrated exact-modulus radius by
\[
W_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\mathfrak R_{n,x}\!\left(P,I_{2,n};t_\alpha\right),
\qquad
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}.
\]
Thus \(W_{n,B_n}\) is a radius quantity computed from the third block of \(B_n\); the associated untruncated symmetric full length is \(2W_{n,B_n}\).

synth_1.title: Full-data response mean
synth_1.body:
For a full-data law package \(P^{\mathrm F}\) with latent-response carrier \(\mathcal U\), latent variable \(U\), structural maps \(g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1]\), and observed stratum \(X\), the full-data response mean in stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\) is
\[
  m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}\{g_x(a,U)\mid X=x\},\qquad a\in[0,1].
\]
When the law package is in the full-data continuity model, the map \(a\mapsto m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\) is continuous on \([0,\bar\delta]\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\).

synth_2.title: Continuity-only regression extension
synth_2.body: For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P\) denotes the unique continuous function on \([0,\bar\delta]\) that agrees, almost everywhere on that interval under the conditional treatment law given \(X=x\), with a version of the conditional mean \(a\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\).

synth_3.title: Observed minimax risk and honest length
synth_3.body:
For the observed clamp target \(\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\) over \(\mathcal M\), the minimax absolute-error risk is
\[
  R_n^\star=\inf_{\widehat\theta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
  \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left|\widehat\theta(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|,
\]
where the infimum ranges over observed-sample measurable estimators taking values in \([0,1]\). The minimax honest expected length is
\[
  L_n^\star=\inf_{C_n:\,\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}P^{\otimes n}\{\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\in C_n\}\ge 1-\alpha}
  \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(C_n)],
\]
where \(C_n\) ranges over observed-sample measurable interval procedures with endpoints in \([0,1]\).

synth_4.title: Total-Gram stabilized estimator
synth_4.body:
Let \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) be a deterministic admissible three-way split, let \(h_n\) be the information-balance bandwidth, and let \(\ell\) be the local-polynomial order. Define the projection
\[
  \operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}(t)=\min\{1,\max\{0,t\}\}.
\]
Set
\[
  \widehat\nu_n=|I_{0,n}|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{0,n}}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\},\qquad
  \widehat b_x=|I_{1,n}|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{1,n}}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\le\delta_n\}.
\]
For each \(x\), let \(\widetilde\mu_x=\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}(\sum_{i\in I_{2,n}}w_{ix}Y_i)\) on \(\Omega_x\), and let \(\widetilde\mu_x=1/2\) on \(\Omega_x^c\). The split-indexed total-Gram estimator is
\[
  \widehat\theta_{n,B_n}^{\mathrm{TG}}
  =\operatorname{clamp}_{[0,1]}\!\left(\widehat\nu_n+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_x\widetilde\mu_x\right).
\]

synth_5.title: Concrete stabilized risk and length
synth_5.body:
For a deterministic admissible split \(B_n\), define the finite-sample worst-case risk of the total-Gram estimator by
\[
  \operatorname{Risk}_n(B_n)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
  \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}\!\left|\widehat\theta_{n,B_n}^{\mathrm{TG}}-\theta_{\delta_n}(P)\right|.
\]
For the bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_{n,B_n}\) formed from the same split, define its worst-case expected length by
\[
  \operatorname{Length}_n(B_n)=\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
  \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_{n,B_n})].
\]

synth_6.title: Projection onto the outcome range
synth_6.body: For a real number \(t\), define \(\Pi_{[0,1]}(t)=\min\{1,\max\{0,t\}\}\). Applied to an estimator or interval endpoint, \(\Pi_{[0,1]}\) denotes this pointwise projection onto the outcome range \([0,1]\).

synth_11.title: Real-to-extended embedding
synth_11.body:
Under the notation and hypotheses of the objects introduced earlier in the paper, a real number \(t\in\mathbb R\) is embedded into the extended nonnegative reals by
\[
t\longmapsto \max\{t,0\}\in[0,\infty]\;.
\]
The image is finite and equals the positive part of \(t\), so real expected-length bounds are compared with extended-real expected lengths through this embedding.

synth_8.title: Admissible three-way split
synth_8.body: At sample size \(n\), an admissible three-way split is a deterministic triple \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) of pairwise-disjoint subsets of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) such that \(|I_j|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\) for \(j=0,1,2\). The blocks are fixed before observing the sample.

synth_10.title: One-cell Bernoulli regressions
synth_10.body: In the one-stratum calibration with \(\beta=\kappa=1\) and \(\pi(a)=2a\), define the null Bernoulli regression by \(m_0(a)=1/2\). For a threshold \(\delta_n\) and bandwidth \(h_n>0\), define the localized alternative by \(m_{1,\delta_n,h_n}(a)=1/2+h_n\,\tau_{\delta_n,h_n}(a)\), where \(\tau_{\delta,h}(a)=\max\{0,1-|a-\delta|/h\}\).

synth_12.title: Bias-aware interval for a fixed split $B_n$
synth_12.body: Let $B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})$ be an admissible deterministic three-way split at sample size $n$. With $h_n$ and $\delta_n$ fixed, form the total-Gram weights $w_{ix}$ and good-design events $\Omega_x$ from the third block $I_{2,n}$. Set $\widehat\nu_{n,B_n}=|I_{0,n}|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{0,n}}Y_i\mathbf 1\{A_i>\delta_n\}$, $\widehat b_{x,B_n}=|I_{1,n}|^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{1,n}}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,A_i\leq\delta_n\}$, and $\widetilde\mu_{x,B_n}=\Pi_{[0,1]}(\sum_{i\in I_{2,n}}w_{ix}Y_i)$ on $\Omega_x$, with $\widetilde\mu_{x,B_n}=1/2$ on $\Omega_x^c$. Define $\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}=\Pi_{[0,1]}\{\widehat\nu_{n,B_n}+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat b_{x,B_n}\widetilde\mu_{x,B_n}\}$. Let $t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}$, $b_{0,B_n}=t_\alpha/\sqrt{|I_{0,n}|}$, and $b_{1,B_n}=t_\alpha/\sqrt{|I_{1,n}|}$. For each $x\in\mathcal X$, set $B_{x,B_n}=Lh_n^\beta\sum_{i\in I_{2,n}}|w_{ix}|+t_\alpha(\sum_{i\in I_{2,n}}w_{ix}^2)^{1/2}$ and $D_{x,B_n}=(\widehat b_{x,B_n}+b_{1,B_n})B_{x,B_n}+b_{1,B_n}$ on $\Omega_x$, while $D_{x,B_n}=\widehat b_{x,B_n}+b_{1,B_n}$ on $\Omega_x^c$. The bias-aware interval formed from $B_n$ is $\mathrm{CI}_{n,B_n}=[\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}-b_{0,B_n}-\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_{x,B_n},\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}+b_{0,B_n}+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}D_{x,B_n}]\cap[0,1]$.

synth_13.title: Observed margin of a full-data law
synth_13.body: For a full-data law package $P^{\mathrm F}$ governing $(X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\})$, define $P^{\mathrm F}_{\mathrm{obs}}$ to be the observed-data marginal law of $(X,A,Y)$. Equivalently, if $\pi_{\mathrm{obs}}(X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a)\})=(X,A,Y)$ is the coordinate projection onto $\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]$, then $P^{\mathrm F}_{\mathrm{obs}}=(\pi_{\mathrm{obs}})_{\#}P^{\mathrm F}$.

synth_16.title: Independent product sample laws
synth_16.body: For an observed-data law \(P\) on \(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]\), write \(P^{\otimes n}\) for the \(n\)-fold product law governing the observed sample \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\), under which the coordinates are independent with common law \(P\). For a full-data law package \(P^{\mathrm F}\), write \((P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}\) for the \(n\)-fold product law governing \(n\) independent full-data draws from \(P^{\mathrm F}\); estimators and intervals indexed by this law are measurable functions of the induced observed coordinates \((O_1,\ldots,O_n)\).

synth_17.title: Length of an observed-sample interval
synth_17.body: For an observed-sample measurable interval \(C_n=C_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)=[\ell_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n),u_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)]\subseteq[0,1]\), define its length pointwise by \(\operatorname{len}(C_n)=u_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)-\ell_n(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\). Thus expected lengths such as \(\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(C_n)]\) are taken with respect to the \(n\)-fold observed-sample law.

synth_18.title: Observed continuity class $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}$
synth_18.body:
Let \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,J\}\), let \(O=(X,A,Y)\in\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1]\), and let \(P\in\mathcal P(\mathcal X\times[0,1]\times[0,1])\). Write
\[
p_x=P(X=x).
\]
The law \(P\) belongs to the continuity-only class \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cont}}\) when, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), the conditional-density condition of \cref{obj:ass:conditional-density-law}, the stratum-mass condition of \cref{obj:ass:stratum-mass}, and the polynomial-thinning condition of \cref{obj:ass:polynomial-thinning} hold, and an almost-everywhere version of \(a\mapsto\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\) has a unique continuous extension
\[
\mu_{x,\mathrm{cont}}^P:[0,\bar\delta]\to[0,1].
\]
The Hölder class \(\mathcal M\) imposes the same three design conditions together with the Hölder regression condition of \cref{obj:ass:holder-regression}; its canonical definition is \cref{obj:def:model-class}, and the canonical continuity-only definition is \cref{obj:def:continuity-model-class}.

synth_19.title: Local-polynomial degree
synth_19.body:
For each smoothness exponent \(\beta\in\mathbb R\), the local-polynomial degree is
\[
\ell(\beta):=\max\{\lceil\beta\rceil_{\mathbb N}-1,0\},
\]
where \(\lceil\beta\rceil_{\mathbb N}\) denotes the least natural number greater than or equal to \(\beta\).

synth_20.title: Exact-modulus interval
synth_20.body:
Assume the notation, model conditions, and preceding constructions in the objects introduced earlier in the paper. Fix an admissible deterministic three-way split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) at sample size \(n\). For a realized observed sample \(z\), let \(\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)\) be the total-Gram estimator formed with the blocks in \(B_n\), and evaluate the realized affine-modulus radius \(R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t_\alpha)\) on the \((X,A)\)-projection of \(z\) using the third block \(I_2\), where
\[
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}.
\]
Define
\[
R_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
R^{\mathrm{ex}}_{z,x}(t_\alpha).
\]
The exact-modulus interval is
\[
C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}(z)
=
\left[
\max\left\{0,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)-R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\},
\min\left\{1,\widehat\theta^{\mathrm{TG}}_{n,B_n}(z)+R_{n,B_n}(z)\right\}
\right].
\]
Its worst-case expected length over the observed-data model is
\[
\ell^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}
\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n}}
\left[
\operatorname{len}\!\left(C^{\mathrm{mod}}_{n,B_n}\right)
\right].
\]

synth_21.title: Exact-modulus radius \(W_{n,B_n}\)
synth_21.body:
Adopt the notation and hypotheses of the objects introduced earlier in the paper.  Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), a deterministic third split block \(I_2\), a stratum \(x\in\mathcal X\), and a multiplier \(t\geq0\).  For a realized design \(z=\{(X_i,A_i):i\in I_2\}\), set
\[
u_i=\frac{A_i-\delta_n}{h_n},
\qquad
S_{z,x}=\{i\in I_2:X_i=x,\ 0\leq u_i\leq1\}.
\]
Let
\[
\mathcal W_{z,x}
=
\left\{
w=(w_i)_{i\in I_2}\in\mathbb R^{I_2}:
w_i=0\ \text{for }i\notin S_{z,x},\
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i u_i^j=\mathbf 1\{j=0\}\ \text{for }j=0,\ldots,\ell
\right\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\) be the class of continuous functions \(f:[0,1]\to[0,1]\) satisfying the declared order-\(\ell\) Hölder Taylor-remainder bound with exponent \(\beta\) and radius \(L\).  For \(w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}\), define the realized Hölder bias functional
\[
B_{z,x}(w)
=
\sup_{f\in\mathcal H_{\beta,L}}
\left|
\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i f(A_i)-f(\delta_n)
\right|.
\]
The realized affine-modulus radius at multiplier \(t\) is
\[
\mathcal R_{z,x}(t)
=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\inf_{w\in\mathcal W_{z,x}}
\left\{
B_{z,x}(w)
+
t\left(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2\right)^{1/2}
\right\},
&\mathcal W_{z,x}\neq\varnothing,\\[1ex]
0,&\mathcal W_{z,x}=\varnothing.
\end{cases}
\]
The integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
\mathfrak R_{n,x}(P,I_2;t)
=
\int
\mathcal R_{z,x}(t)\,
\mathrm d(P_{X,A}^{\otimes I_2})(z),
\]
where \(P_{X,A}^{\otimes I_2}\) is the independent observed-design product law on the coordinates in \(I_2\).

If \(B_n=(I_{0,n},I_{1,n},I_{2,n})\) is an admissible deterministic three-way split at sample size \(n\), its worst integrated exact-modulus radius is
\[
W_{n,B_n}
=
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}
\mathfrak R_{n,x}\!\left(P,I_{2,n};t_\alpha\right),
\qquad
t_\alpha=\sqrt{\log(12J/\alpha)/2}.
\]
Thus \(W_{n,B_n}\) is a radius quantity computed from the third block of \(B_n\), and the associated untruncated symmetric full length is \(2W_{n,B_n}\).
